en: May there be auspiciousness unto the dweller of glorious Vaikuṇṭha, the abode of Śrī, the Creator,
the bearer of the conch, discus, mace, and lotus, who wears a garland of forest flowers. 1.
Salutations to the bestower of the desires of devotees, who possesses an auspicious form and wields the Śārṅga bow;
to the one initiated in the protection of the fallen, whose nature is that of the Supreme Self;
and to the supreme Lord of the gods, who consists of the forms of creation, preservation, and dissolution.
Salutations again and again to Mādhava, whose form is the beginning of the Fish and other incarnations.
Once, the silent sage Nārada was wandering through the three worlds,
[passing through regions] filled with various trees, creepers, and shrubs, and teeming with various wild animals.
The great bank of the Bhāgīrathī was always delightful, frequented by various flowers and fruits as well as birds of many species;
it was inhabited by the foremost of sages and was the destroyer of great sins.
Having gone there and bathed with great devotion, and having meditated upon Janārdana,
he bowed according to the prescribed rites to the lords of the self-restrained who were stationed there;
then the lord of sages, bowing low with devotion, spoke these words to them.
"O best of Brahmins, for what purpose have you come here?
What are you all doing in this place? Tell me everything in detail.
Thus addressed, all the sages were delighted in their hearts.
Beholding the most excellent of celestial sages and bowing down to him again and again, they addressed these words to him by way of what is about to be said:
"O Blessed One, knower of all dharmas, O Nārada, bull among the twice-born! (9-10)
We have all been purified by the very sight of you;
moreover, this hermitage of ours has become supremely sanctified by the dust of your lotus feet. Indeed, you are the fruit of our ascetic penance.
"O great-souled one, O crest-jewel of sages, this very essence has indeed been cultivated by us.
Formerly, all the Vedas were studied by us in their entirety, as well as their auxiliary limbs and other scriptures in detail. (12-13)
But our state of being established in Brahman has not been attained by anyone at all;
therefore, desiring to know that which is so difficult to cross, we have come here.
Because he performed penance for a long time, Śaṅkara became pleased in his mind.

O Sage, the Lord, accompanied by Pārvatī, became manifest before our very eyes. By His grace, we— who have been initiated into His conduct— have attained some measure of realization through this great scripture of the single path.
O Sage, although we have made our dwelling here on the banks of the Bhāgīrathī,
certain doubts regarding the worship of Hari and other matters enjoined by the scriptures of the Blessed One continue to arise within us now. (17)
O Nārada, you alone are worthy of preventing them;
for among those on earth who know all dharmas as proclaimed in the Śruti of the Ekāyana, there is no one equal to you in this world, whether in debate or in reflection. (18–19)
"Therefore, by the very path prescribed in the illustrious Sāṃcarātra scripture,
please show us compassion and dispel the web of our doubts. Thus entreated, the ocean of mercy looked upon those sages who were observing a vow of silence.
Nārada, who is supremely devoted, spoke thus:
"Listen, all you sages, to that which you desire;
I shall speak according to my ability the secret of the Lord's scripture."
Formerly, this great scripture was heard by my father, the Creator, in the city of Vaikuṇṭha, out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds.
[It was spoken by] the glorious Nārāyaṇa, Śauri, Hari, the Supreme Puruṣa.
During five nights, he himself recounted all of that even to Brahmā;
subsequently, I too have studied this entire work in its entirety from my ancestors—
the supreme means for the worship of Śrī Viṣṇu, along with its secret doctrines.

"Having understood this, O sages, those men who are immersed in the awakening of non-becoming on this earth will attain the eternal abode of Śrī Hari; of this there is no doubt. To the wise Nārada, the best of sages, as he was speaking thus—
Seeing them, the sages, who were dear to the Blessed One, became joyful in heart;
having seated him in the hermitage and first offered the guest-offering (arghya) and water for the feet (pādya),
they honored him with fruits, tubers, roots, and honey.
Having given [the offerings] on that earth according to the rules, yet without full satisfaction,
they sat down and meditated in their hearts upon the Lord Janārdana; then,
one by one, they began to ask about their various doubts.
Thus ends the first chapter, titled "The Introduction of the Scripture," in the Paramapuruṣasaṃhitā, which is the essence of the secret teachings of the Śrī Pāñcarātra. The sages said:
"O Blessed One, O tiger among sages, you who are highly proficient in the Pāñcarātra."
Please command us regarding the supreme determination of the number of worshippers and others;
what distinction has been declared for the group of attendants, and at what time should that supreme determination for them be performed?
Śrī Nārada said: "For the sake of increasing their families, what means were raised? Pray, tell us their characteristics in detail."
Listen, all you sages, with minds filled with devotion,
to that which was fashioned for the abode of Hari for the prosperity of the king and his kingdom,
so that the worship of the Slayer of Madhu may continue uninterrupted as long as the moon and sun endure.
On the day of the installation, other priests who have reached a definitive conclusion [regarding the ritual] should be appointed—

those who know the truth of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, who are of virtuous conduct, who have mastered devotion, who are devoted to recitation, fire-offerings, and so forth, who are young, and who speak the truth. || 5-6 ||
[He saw] those Śrīvaiṣṇavas who were endowed with fear of sin, possessed of the five purificatory rites (saṃskāras), initiated, experts in the Pāñcarātra system,
knowers of other tantras, and well-trained in the renunciation of self-interest.
[He saw] those whose every limb was complete, whose bodies were always free from disease,
who through their ancestral lineage were solely devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu;
and even if these great devotees were not present, [he saw] the twice-born [in their stead].
[He saw] those endowed with the fivefold ritual observances, skilled in the knowledge of the Nāgas,
whose minds were always intent on the meditation and worship of Hari,
who were supremely devoted to the One, and dedicated to the five daily rites.

One should first select one hundred and eight, or thirty-two, or twenty-four, or even sixteen priests who are devoted to virtuous conduct and endowed with all the previously mentioned characteristics.
There should be sixteen, twelve, or eight officiants, or even just two; or at the very least, one, according to the capacity of the patron.
He may be a celibate student, a householder, a forest-dweller, or an ascetic.
In a sacrifice for a *parārdha* [of years], one is indeed worthy of worshipping Viṣṇu; of this there is no doubt.

(14) If one who is without the sacred thread (*anupavītī*) or without a wife should worship in the temple, there will surely be the destruction of that region and the extinction of the king's lineage. (15)
One who is uninitiated, lacking in proper conduct, devoid of the five purificatory rites (saṃskāras), physically impaired, afflicted by disease, born of a low lineage,
a heretic, ignorant of the scriptures, and not a Vaiṣṇava— such a person is the lowest among men. || 16 ||
If one worships Hari himself out of greed for wealth from that country,
then a constant misfortune for that country arises for foreigners; he is known as a *vaidehalaka*, excluded from all ritual acts.
O lords of sages, among worshippers on earth, he who performs service to another [deity] and so forth shall incur terrible sin merely by the sight of that [true worshipper];
such a person is declared to be a Chandala.
One may obtain some fruit from the worship performed by others; however,

having observed the superiority of the sacred field, the twice-born worshippers must be determined according to their respective lineages, even if they are of different gotras, and in accordance with the extent of their available wealth.
He should provide for the increase of their family by granting them a permanent dwelling that extends through the succession of their lineage;
then the sacrificer, with a serene mind, establishes himself before the deity.
By the command of the preceptor alone, having summoned a twice-born man who is pure and present nearby at an auspicious moment, and having paid obeisance according to the rules,
"O bull among the twice-born, accept this land given by me for the sake of propitiating the Lord and for the prosperity of your family.
Having been thus informed, the donor, with a truly gracious heart, [accepted].
"There is no doubt that the worshipper is Hari himself in visible form.
Thinking thus in his heart, he bowed his head to the ground before the worshipper and offered him earth from the hand [of the image], along with gold, fruit, and water.
Having given the gift of land according to the prescribed rite in the presence of the deity,
and having inscribed the deed of gift upon a stone slab or a copper plate,
it should be presented to the officiating priest with a completely pure mind.
Whoever performs this with a serene mind according to this rite,
not only do those born in his lineage— hundreds before him and hundreds after him— attain the supreme state,
but the performer of the worship of the Blessed One likewise attains it through this very procedure.
One should perform only the gift of land, and never a hired service;
if one performs a hired service without the gift of land,
his lineage shall perish, and his life and prosperity shall vanish.
O best of the twice-born, he who accepts wages for the worship of Hari is declared a *devalaka*,
excluded from all ritual acts;
therefore, with every effort, one should cause land alone to be given [as a gift].
O Blessed One, those who, having written down this supreme teaching on giving, should cause it to be presented to a priest under the name of the Blessed One—
for them, the gift of land in the name of the gods is declared to be the most excellent. (34)
The middle name of the officiating priest shall be the bestower of fruit.
If the builder should write only his own name for the sake of the highest merit, he alone shall be the builder of the Lord’s temple. (35-36)
If, having fashioned it, one then takes that image of the deity and receives something, whether it be a small gift or even a slight injury;
or if, perceiving it to be full of poison, one should cause it to be given to the worshippers (arcakas).
Having performed this great renunciation, the doer shall immediately attain glory.
But that lowest of men who, out of delusion, consumes even a tiny portion of the deity’s property shall go to the terrible hells, such as Śālmali and others.
Therefore, one who is free from desire should install Lord Hari with every effort;
thereafter, for the sake of serving the water from the holy feet of the Blessed One,
one should appoint a Sthānācārya and a Hastaka in that place.
Born of a noble lineage, truthful, virtuous, and a performer of good deeds;
(41) of excellent conduct, a true devotee, and always devoted to Hari; free from anger, greed, pride, and the like—he is indeed the best of Vaiṣṇavas. (42)

He was a knower of the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences (vedāṅgas), devoted to austerity and self-study, conversant with the rules of the Pañcarātra, initiated through the five purificatory rites (saṃskāras),
a knower of the dharma of the five times (pañcakālika), and the most excellent among those of supreme single-minded devotion.
With all his limbs complete and a body always free from disease,
he should be pure, advanced in age, an embodiment of compassion, and a teacher established in his station;
according to the very procedure handed down through the lineage, he should remain in the presence of Hari.
The Guru himself should first receive the grace of the Lord’s sacred ford and reside there for a full day and night;
beginning at sunrise until the conclusion of the worship.
At the commencement of the Brahmotsava and other such rites, his formal installation is performed.

Whether he be a student, a householder, or an ascetic, provided he is endowed with the requisite characteristics, he shall be the Sthānācārya; this is the certain conclusion of the scriptures. (47-48)

If a *yati* (ascetic) is declared to be the highest, the householder (*gṛhastha*) is remembered as middling, and the student (*brahmacārī*) as the lowest; such is the determination regarding their status as teachers.
If a *yati* should be the presiding authority over the site, then out of respect, half of that settlement [should be granted] to him.
Whether in the second enclosure or even in the third enclosure,
having constructed a single monastery, it should be given according to the donor's wish;
by the tradition of the monastery, the principal disciple shall become the Guru.
If he is an ascetic named Madha, or even a householder with that name, one should designate for him a village or land yielding half his livelihood.
Furthermore, according to the extent of the field, there may be one, two, or three Vaiṣṇavas.
Having determined the office of the Sthānācārya immediately thereafter,
[one should perform] the daily recitation of the Vedas, the teaching of the scriptures, the chanting of the Prastotra, and the recitation of the Drāviḍa-āmnāya in the presence of the Deity. (53–54)
One should choose the teachers from among the lower classes by the very same method previously described— whether it be a thousand,
ten thousand, a hundred, or even one hundred and eight;
or a number of seventy-four, or thirty-two, according to the rule.
Twelve, eight, four, and then four again for the lowest of the low;
one should invite the teachers together with the presiding lord to all the temples, as this is remembered as the primary method of instruction. || 56–57 ||
Just as the nourishment of the body is called the primary [duty],
so too is the daily recitation of the hymn (stotra) by the teachers always declared to be the primary [duty]. The number of these teachers shall be ten thousand, divine and supreme.
Counting the collection of one thousand names constitutes the most excellent of the excellent (uttamottama). Counting one hundred and eight names is said to be the excellent-middle (uttamamadhyama),
while counting seventy-four names is declared to be the excellent-low (uttamādhamam).
The number of thirty-two services is called the highest-middling;
the number of twenty-four names is the middling-middling. With sixteen services, it is called the lowest-middling.
That which is numbered by the sages (seven) beginning with the elements (five) is declared to be the lowest of the high (adhamottama).
That which is numbered by the eight directions is said to be the middle of the low (adhamamadhyama).
And that which is numbered by the [four] vyūhas is called the lowest of the low (adhamādhamanāmaka).
Thus have these reciters been described in the ritual for the worship of Viṣṇu;
by them, in the home of the God of gods, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, the auspicious Vedas, scriptures, hymns, and so forth, should always be recited. (64)
In all the divine fields,
one should establish a group of teachers of the highest of the high order, which brings happiness to all the world;
if one is unable to do so, one should appoint those of lower or higher numbers according to one's capacity.
One should choose excellent teachers; therefore, one should not cause them to do little work.
One should place the Ṛgveda in the eastern direction, the Yajurveda in the south, the Sāmaveda in the west, and likewise the Atharvaveda in the north.
One should recite the Itihāsa in the southeast and the Stotra in the southwest (68).
The Dharmaśāstra is prescribed for the northwest, and the Āgama for the northeast; one should cause each of these, including the Drāviḍa-Āmnāya, to be recited in each of the four directions (69).
Twelve teachers, numbering twelve syllables, should always,
day and night, with a perfectly pure mind, pray to the Lord of Gods for the protection of the world and for the increase of the kingdom and the nation. || 70 ||
During the time of their pilgrimage, they must dwell near Hāri;
otherwise, the pilgrimage does not purify those village-dwellers.
Therefore, one should [worship] only them—the Bhūtas, Sarovara, Yogīśvara, and the others.
Thinking thus and honoring them, the world will attain certainty that they shall cross over; moreover, the first act of hospitality toward them is prescribed even in the temple of the gods.
First, one should satisfy them with the waters of the Hariprasāda-tīrtha and other such sacred sites.
For the sake of their livelihood, the patron (yajamāna) should provide either land or a salary;
of these two, land is considered the best, while a salary is the lowest. || 74-75 ||
Therefore, with every effort, one should cause land to be granted to the officiating priest for half his share, for the sake of assistance in the rites of the deity day and night,
as well as for the purpose of cleaning vessels and the like, and for half the cost of lighting lamps. || 76 ||
For the purpose of moving the hand-bell and for sprinkling water, there should be a place and so forth.
There shall be two Vaiṣṇavas for each one Brāhmaṇa priest;
they must be pure and endowed with all the characteristics required of those who serve as priests.
The *hastakauvara* should determine their land or wages according to their capacity, with devotion by the sacrificer;
this applies to the task of cooking the oblation for the God of gods three times a day.
Or else, twelve or nine Vaiṣṇavas— numbering six or three—

who are cooks endowed with the required characteristics, who are skilled in the culinary arts according to the previously mentioned procedure, must be determined as appropriate for the wealth [of the patron]. (80–81)

O twice-born ones, at the time of offering the oblation, those who have bound their nostrils with a cloth should proceed until the end of the food offering (naivedya), remaining filled with fear and devotion;
during the previously mentioned times, all conversation must be abandoned.
O best of the twice-born, for their livelihood, one should provide either land or a salary, having considered one's own capacity; this must be determined after careful deliberation.
[One should also provide] musical instruments such as the bherī, mṛdaṅga, paṭaha, vīṇā, veṇu, and others.
[He saw] those who sounded bells, kahalas, trumpets, and the like, and those who produced the sound of mṛdaṅga drums;
those skilled in dance, song, and so forth; bards, panegyrists, and scribes; soldiers with canes in their hands; and the keepers of elephants, horses, camels, and other animals. || 85 ||
He likewise appointed cowherds, temple-servants, and charioteers;
those who ensured the purity of the sacrificial vessels and the purity of the ritual implements; as well as those who carried the parasols, fly-whisks, and staffs, and the bearers of these items.

O best of the wise, it is said that all these servants, endowed with the five purificatory rites (pañcasaṃskāra), should be employed according to their capacity for the sake of increasing the worship of the Lord;
yet others who are unworthy remain excluded from the abode of Hari.
Having determined what is appropriate for their livelihood— whether land or a wage—
the patron, with a serene mind, should then appoint them to those specific tasks that have been decided upon. (89-90)
He who, according to the procedure thus described and by the path taught in the Pañcarātra, has the Lord Hari installed by a group of attendants,
goes to the supreme abode, which is difficult even for yogins to attain.
That place is truly the city of Vaikuṇṭha, and the Blessed Lord resides there as if present in person.
According to the wealth of the patron, one should arrange for all these [officiants];
otherwise, one should choose at least a single worshipper out of a spirit of devotion.

If the patron is unable [to perform the full rite], he shall obtain the complete fruit by establishing two priests and worshipping Śauri according to the prescribed rules. This applies even at the time of the restoration of a dilapidated temple of the Enemy of Madhu (Viṣṇu). || 94 ||
In a place honored by sages and others, having explained the sequence of the lineage,
the king should not perform any special act— whether out of anger, greed, delusion, or even through negligence— for the sake of the prosperity of the kingdom and its people. (95–96)
It is taught that for whoever creates a division in this [tradition] which has come down through successive lineage in all divine fields, there shall be the destruction of their own lineage.
One should not cause an increase or decrease in the number of attendants.
Excess is declared to be fruitless, while deficiency brings about the destruction of the world.
Therefore, with every effort, one should not allow for either deficiency or excess.
Thus ends the excellent determination regarding the number of priests and other attendants.
"This supreme secret was previously spoken by Hari himself to the Lotus-born [Brahmā] in brief; today it has been revealed by me to you.
Thus ends the second chapter, titled "The Determination of the Number of Priests, Attendants, and Others," in the *Paramapuruṣasaṃhitā*, the essence of the secret teachings of the *Śrī Pāñcarātra*.
O sage Maunīcandra, O highly fortunate one, you who are ever devoted to Hari;
why have you constructed a temple for the God of gods, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow?
Upon its consecration, the builder should then grant that temple to someone;
who shall then become the perpetual superintendent (adhikārī) of Hari from that time forward, during all the daily and occasional rites of worship and at all festivals?
2. During the rites known as nitya and naimittika, and in all festivals...
"O treasure-house of mercy, tell us all that in detail.
Śrī Nārada said:
"I shall relate it to you in full; listen with devotion."
O sages, you whose minds are fixed on the Supreme Lord and devoted to His scriptures, O highly fortunate ones, I shall now speak that which is to be kept secret;
O twice-born ones, one should never speak this to one who is not a devotee nor to one who is not a disciple.
The worshipper of the illustrious Śauri is undoubtedly like a son;
therefore, he alone should be the patron in all rites within the temple of the Blessed One during the entire range of activities beginning with worship. 6.
The group of attendants and likewise his servants should always act according to the instructions of the officiating priest (arcaka),
whether they are born from the family of the patron (yajamāna) or descended from a determined lineage.

If there is even a single superintendent of religious affairs (dharmādhīkārī), he too, in accordance with the instructions of the officiating priest (arcaka), shall always summon the servants and assign them their appropriate duties. 9.
He shall summon them and direct their suitable tasks.

In that same manner, having prepared at the proper time the materials suitable for worship— such as perfumes, flowers, fruits, and so forth— one should cause them to be presented to the officiant. Furthermore,
whenever any faults are observed among the attendants, [one should address them].
Therefore, the wise man should always punish those who act with transgression; however,
O twice-born ones, when there is some fault or the like among the group of attendants of the deity,
the authority to inflict punishment belongs to anyone at all.
Then Hari himself will grant them hell; or else, out of a sense of being their son, Hari will indeed forgive them. Therefore, he considers that Hari is the direct fulfiller of their purpose.
Since the examination of the faults of the worshipper is prescribed, therefore, even for a slight fault in worship and so forth, the worshipper shall go to hell. 15.
If the worshipper commits even a minor fault in the act of worship and so forth...
He attains the training appropriate for that [state] even in this very life, without a doubt.
Therefore, a worshiper should always conduct himself with devotion, with great reverence and fear, in the temple of the Blessed One, maintaining the attitude of a servant to his Lord.
Whoever performs the worship of Lord Viṣṇu, the enemy of Madhu,
with devotion, faith, and solely with the thought of the Supreme,
having abandoned their own self-interest out of a desire for the welfare of all the worlds— || 18 ||
He indeed shall become blessed and honored, and shall attain both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
O sages,
best of the twice-born, most excellent of munis, you who are proficient in the meaning of all the scriptures!
Why do you proclaim the preeminence of those who worship in the abode of Viṣṇu?
How will they on this earth accept all the garments, ornaments, and other gifts offered by devotees in the temple of the Blessed Lord? (20-21)
O Sage, for what purpose were these all-authorized ones created,
and for what purpose does the world always worship them with devotion and faith?
Tell us this and whatever else we have not asked in detail.
"Speak to us, O highly fortunate one, if there is compassion for us;
O Śrī Nārada,
O best of sages, you have been well-asked regarding that which is desired and dear to us."
I shall now speak in brief; listen with attention.
All the gods, beginning with Viṣṇu, are understood to be presided over by mantras;
it is through the accomplishment of those very mantras that they possess divine temples and forms.
The worshippers establish the Lord of Gods and make him firm, for all mantras always proceed under his authority.
He who knows the Āgamas is worthy of worship; such a priest is equal to the Blessed One himself.
If even one person among them is devoid of devotion, all the temple servants, along with their wealth,
jewels, grain, and other possessions, are considered to have perished for nothing.
Therefore, at the conclusion of the consecration, the builder should indeed construct a house for the Blessed Lord.

One who causes the worshipper to be endowed with all the necessary requisites and provides the image of the body [of the deity] is considered the presiding lord of the worshipper of Viṣṇu; such a person becomes entirely independent and shall be the worshipper in the temple of the Blessed Lord.
It should be understood that no one among those engaged in Vedic rituals and the like is capable of commanding him,
whether as an agent or otherwise;
just as all the servants in a temple are filled with devotion.
The superintendent of the temple shall carry out the command of the Dharmādhikārin, held upon his head;
likewise, the officiant (arcaka), while obeying the command of the superintendent,
shall always provide all the materials for worship at the proper time.
In all Ālayas, the worship prescribed by the scriptures should always be performed.
One [form of worship] is declared to be the most principal; the others are all the grandeur of festivals, existing as subsidiary parts for the sake of causing people to hear [the teachings]. 33–34.
Therefore, O weaver, in the house of this very Lord Hari, let there be worship performed according to the capacity of the patron,
accompanied by all divine splendors and festivals; or else, even if devoid of such splendors, let there be the supreme worship as prescribed in the scriptures.
However, one person must be appointed for the prosperity of the king and the kingdom.
Just as in the world the vital breath is said to be the chief of the body, so too, according to the scriptures, the minister should be the foremost of the state.
Just as ornaments are for the sake of the beauty of a living body,
so too should all festive enjoyments in the house of the Blessed One, which is endowed with the worship prescribed by the scriptures, be regarded as being for the sake of beauty. 38.
Just as an ornament does not shine upon a body devoid of life, even so, O best of the twice-born, the grandeur of festivals does not shine upon an image that is deficient;
this is the certain truth.

Whatever is most essential to the Ālaya should be offered as worship by the attendants; for that reason, the attendants should please the one dear to the Blessed One with all kinds of pleasant speech, and with gifts such as cattle, land, gold, and clothing.
The worshipper is the son of the Lord;

having always accepted everything offered to the Lord for the sake of the welfare of the world, he shall himself bestow blessings upon his progenitor, Hari, after praying to Him while seated in the presence of the Lord.

The complete satisfaction of the priest is declared to be the satisfaction of the Lord; his grace is certainly the grace of Śrī Viṣṇu. By the power of that very [grace], there shall be happiness for all the worlds.
O best of sages, this subtle dharma has been proclaimed in this world:
if a man, being angry, reviles the son of Hari, the destroyer of Mura, may he become a reviler of the Blessed One, and the destruction of his lineage is certain. (45-46)
In whatever place the priest is angry, there Śauri becomes angry; therefore, men should always act in every way for the sake of pleasing the Blessed One,
offering all things to the priests with the disposition of dedicating them to Hari.

In rites such as marriages and other ceremonies, one should satisfy him on all festival days. If the officiating priest becomes angry and pronounces a curse, that kingdom, its king, and all its people perish instantly.
Whatever wealth, clothing, fruits, and so forth are offered to the Blessed One,
their acceptance by the priest constitutes the direct possession of Hari himself.
In that case, it is said that there is no violation of the priest’s means of livelihood.
In that regard, worship performed with a mind devoid of faith should be known as futile. Where there is an omission of worship, all of that is recorded as futile;
the kingdom will not prosper, and even the deity will become angry.
Therefore, he who causes a division through causes such as anger, passion, or greed, or through the consumption of impure food, shall suffer the destruction of his lineage.
His ancestors are said to attain the state of Daityas, and his birth is recorded as that of a Piśāca.
A slayer of a Brahmin, a drinker of spirituous liquor, a thief of gold, and one who has killed his wife—[the merit of this gift] is equal to [the expiation for] these;
no such terrible sin exists on earth.
This subtle principle of Dharma should be known by all human beings.
Since the worshipper of the Lord alone is the cause of the world's welfare,
therefore, O best of sages, people on earth always worship Him;
having made Him gracious and fully satisfied, the world proceeds.
Since he is always to be worshipped by the worshipper solely with the spirit of Hari, therefore he alone should be the first object of worship in the assembly;
provided that, in the house of the Lord, he has installed an image with effort. || 57-58 ||
It is certain that at no time will anyone be able to rescue [the deity] from that state;
indeed, at the conclusion of the ritual, it must be firmly resolved by the sacrificer, or by the priest, or even by those related to them.
59. Or [it may be resolved] by the worshipper, or by his kin, or at any time whatsoever.
The sacrificer himself is unable to prevent it.
If anyone should act thus out of anger or other motives, his lineage shall perish;
at that time, there will certainly be misfortune for the country and suffering for the subjects.
If the image-maker or the worshipper dies, a re-consecration must be performed;
therefore, from the day of the consecration until the dissolution of the world,
one should maintain a single lineage of worshippers for the image of Hari in the temple.
The priest shall daily perform the festivals and other rites within the abode of Hari throughout the day and night, according to the path prescribed in the scriptures;
therefore, he shall indeed reside in the vicinity of the temple of the Lord.
In the second enclosure or even in the third enclosure,
having set aside a single house endowed with all auspicious characteristics and adorned with serpent-like beauty, one should cause it to be given as a gift for the body of the image.
Since Pūjara is declared to be the direct son of the Blessed One,
one should therefore conceive of his family as divine; thus, there is no fault even in the case of the deities in the palaces and enclosures.
O best of sages, O protectors of dharma, whether it be the officiating priest, the builder of the temple, the patron,
or anyone else who is involved in the construction of the enclosure for the abode of Śauri, [they all share in the merit]. || 68 ||

O best of sages, it is certain that Hariṣca becomes enraged when he makes his dwelling in a place; he brings destruction to that region, and there will surely be plague in the village and the ruin of that person's lineage. 69–70.

Without the acceptance by the officiating priest, the grace of the Lord cannot come to pass; however, it is said that one should take half the portion for oneself and give the other half to the devotees.
(71) Without the acceptance by the officiating priest, it is not called His grace.
Whoever consumes it out of delusion will certainly incur sin.
But that which is offered by the worshipper is a sacred place endowed with greatness;
by drinking it, a person obtains long life, health, liberation, and other blessings.
During times of great festivals and the like, the worshipper of the God of gods, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, should always speak to all the priests while in His very presence; likewise,
the worshipper [should remain] near the God of gods, even when attending to His vehicles and other such items.
One should serve him with the duties of holding the umbrella and the fly-whisk; indeed, one should praise him.
Having adorned oneself with auspicious garments, ornaments, and the like, those who carry the two attendants and Śauri mounted upon a vehicle [attain great merit]. 75–76.
Those who remain on the earth for even a single moment while carrying the Lord go to the supreme Vaikuṇṭha, liberated from all sins;
they obtain the merit of circumambulating the entire earth— of this there is no doubt.
Even the touch of Śrī Hari’s vehicle bestows liberation. However, a devotee who is favored by the gods and accompanied by the goddesses is a manifest deity in this world, bestowing all happiness.
O Lord, the majesty of the worshipper is indeed remembered as the greatness of the Blessed One;
without the worshipper, there is neither the God nor His temple.
Certainly, there is no worship, no festival, and no greatness.
Therefore, he is called Śrī-Yanārdana by the worshipper alone. One should always cause the food offered [to the Lord] to be given to the worshippers;
for the worshipper should always consume the food offered to the Blessed One.
If one, out of delusion, eats the food of others and then worships the Lord of the Universe, his worship on this earth shall be fruitless.
Therefore, with every effort, [one should offer] the entire oblation (naivedya).
If there is more, one should give half a portion, or even a fourth part;
first, however, having given to the *tvarcaka*s, it should be given to others.
That which is the *naivedya* offered in the temple of the Lord must not be given to anyone other than the *tvarcaka*s.
That [food] must always be abandoned by devotees as if it were poison;
for if one eats it out of mere greed, his previous merit perishes.
This applies both when entering the inner sanctum and while sitting or reclining there.
O Brahmins,
just as Vāsuki, the king of serpents, is terrified upon seeing a staff-bearing messenger on earth,
so too is Janārdana terrified upon seeing a priest who is devoid of mantras, even if that priest is appointed and honored according to all the scriptures. (87-88)

Therefore, one who worships and is intent on the practice of mantras should always remain on this earth; otherwise, he shall go to hell. (89) The attainment [of merit] consists of all food and other offerings given by true devotees in the temples of the gods.
It is the settled conclusion in the scriptures as to which worshipers are worthy to accept [offerings].
Therefore, O best of sages, it is certain that even if one possesses much wealth, if he takes anything from that [forbidden source] on earth, his lineage will quickly perish. 90–91.
If the patron, having taken possession of that wealth, performs festivals and other such activities out of greed, he is remembered as a *vṛthā-yajvan* (one who sacrifices in vain).
If the patron is incapable of maintaining the temple of Hari, [he is likewise considered a vṛthā-yajvan].
One should perform all duties solely by means of wandering for alms.
Thus, O twice-born ones, the reason for the preeminence of the *arcaka* has been correctly explained; it was previously told to my father by the Blessed One himself. 93–94.
"In brief, all of this has been well-expounded for you;
the wise should never speak it to one who is not a devotee, nor to one who is not a disciple.

(95) Thus ends the third chapter, titled "The Determination of the Superiority of the Worshipper," in the *Śrī-paramapuruṣa-saṃhitā*, which is the essence of the secret teachings of the *Śrī-pāñcarātra*.
O Blessed One, O master of all scriptures, we sages desire to hear about the greatness of Hari’s grace and the particular excellence of that sacred ford.
O Sage, what fruit does one obtain on this earth by beholding the Blessed One and by worshipping Him with perfumes, flowers, fruits, and the like, as well as garments, ornaments, and other offerings,
and by dedicating them to Viṣṇu?
O Sage, please tell me in detail out of compassion: what is the fruit of performing great festivals and the like, as well as the restoration of ruined temples? Thus [asked] Śrī Nārada.
"Listen today, O sages, with minds endowed with devotion.
I shall explain to you in detail that which you desire to know: the offering of food to the Blessed One, including all types of eatables, lickables, and so forth, at all times."
That which is given during the *Tvarcaka* [period] is called divine grace (*divyaprasāda*);
indeed, by accepting it, a man becomes free from all poisons. At whatever time one receives this grace from the Lord of the Worlds, [it is most auspicious].
"O best of sages, accept this very moment and eat!
He who eats the food of Hari every day with a spirit of devotion shall enjoy all pleasures in this world and, at the end, attain Vaikuṇṭha. (7-8)
O best of sages, without considering whether it is tainted by defects of vision or defects of touch, this prasāda must be accepted by everyone in the temple;
for whoever creates a division in this matter, his lineage shall come to ruin.
But he who reviles the Prasāda shall certainly go to hell.
O wise ones, one should not abandon the Prasāda even on the Ekādaśī day;
having fasted, one may eat a single grain held upon the head.
All those who observe the vows beginning with Ekādaśī do so out of love for Hari;
therefore, on those days, the acceptance of prasāda is auspicious.
He who does not consume prasāda due to reasons such as anger or greed [is at fault].
That lowest of men who remains devoted to vows and fasts alone,
O best of the wise, all his vows become fruitless,
even when auspicious acts are offered to Viṣṇu at times dedicated to his father, mother, or preceptor.
The performer should especially worship the ancestors with food and other offerings with great devotion;
O twice-born ones, by that, the ancestors quickly attain a good state.
The invited Brahmins and the performer [should remain] in the temple of Hari during the Śrāddha.
Having drunk the *tīrtha* water, one should offer that grace (*prasāda*) to the devotees.
On whatever day one partakes of the grace of Viṣṇu,
whether at an improper time or even at the right time, one is liberated from all anxiety.

When, due to causes such as the loss of faith, devotion, and reverence, whatever [offering] falls upon that [deity] is considered to bring ruin to the village. He who eats the food of Hari is certainly a drinker of Soma.
He who eats it for three days shall possess a healthy body;
and by eating this constantly, one shall attain Vaikuṇṭha,
whether desiring liberation, desiring a residence [there], or for whatever reason whatsoever.

O best of sages, whoever gives as an offering half of the food, grain, or even wealth belonging to Hari, shall possess great wealth. In this world, he shall have grain and other riches, and at the end, he shall attain the presence of Lord Viṣṇu.
If one should give even a small gift dear to Hari with great devotion,
or even half of the food offering according to one's ability, he too shall attain Vaikuṇṭha—
He in whose belly all the worlds always abide.
O lords of sages, because Viṣṇu is never satiated, the offering of that food (naivedya) leads to the satisfaction of all the worlds. If Śauri,
who dwells within all bodies, is satisfied by that offering, [then all are satisfied].
All the worlds are satisfied; there is no need for further deliberation on this matter.
From the kitchen up to the presence of the Blessed One, may they be honored along the way with umbrellas, chowries, and lamps.
Then Pācaka was honored with the sounds of all musical instruments, auspicious Vedic chants, hymns of praise, and every kind of ritual service;
he was held over his head, being entirely free from any defects such as physical touch or the gaze of others.
Having brought [the offerings] to the pavilion for enjoyment while recollecting the King of Mantras (Maṃtrarāja),
he should sprinkle them with devotion and place them before Hari,
whether they be uncooked, cooked, or infested with worms, insects, and the like.
That which is excessively hot or excessively cold, that which is prepared by one who is not a Vaiṣṇava,
that which has been seen by a Śūdra or a Caṇḍāla, or touched by crows, dogs, and the like; that which is devoid of flavor, or offered to another deity— [these are unfit].

One should never offer to Śauri, the God of gods, that which is contaminated by hair, insects, and the like; defiled by liquor, meat, and so forth; smelled; stepped over; or fallen upon the ground. || 31-32 ||
Alternatively, if one should offer food possessed of defects to the Lord of Śrī,
one should immediately perform a bath and carry out a propitiatory fire-sacrifice (śānti-homa).
O twice-born ones, all vessels suitable for cooking the sacrificial oblation (havis) [must be used].

One should mark oneself with the conch, the discus, the vertical tilaka (ūrdhvapuṇḍra), and other signs by way of devotion. Men should never eat any food cooked on earth that has been offered to Hari before it has first become *naivedya* (the food offered to the deity).
O twice-born ones, if one eats out of delusion, his life-span and prosperity perish;

however, that food which has been cooked for the purpose of an offering (naivedya) is not defiled by that act, provided it is indeed intended for the offering. If it were defiled even before the offering was made, then it would be so.

One should first pour water over the food according to the prescribed rule and then cook it. He who eats that food without having poured water over it shall experience all manner of miseries in this world and then go to the Raurava hell.
He who eats the prasāda in the temple of the Blessed One for six months—
his sins all perish, of this there is no doubt.
He who eats the food of the naivedya in the abode of Hari for one year [attains the same].

The wise attain the arising of knowledge and steadfastness in Brahman through him. But if one partakes of the grace of the God residing in the *radha*, she shall certainly become the mother of a son within a short time; this is certain.
O best of sages, she who, desiring offspring on the birthday of Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
drinks cow’s milk offered to Vāsudeva on this earth,
shall certainly become possessed of excellent sons.
At the time of ascending the throne, it was declared by Vainateya:
"The woman who eats the mudga-bean rice shall become possessed of sons;
and the remnant offered to the devotees is a divine grace that grants the attainment of liberation."
Food offered to the Lord of the World during the month of Māgha at the time of sunrise is remembered as yielding a thousandfold fruit.
Whatever is offered by all devotees when a great festival is underway [is likewise meritorious].

The offering of food (naivedya) to Viṣṇu alone is the cause for attaining Vaikuṇṭha. That noble person who constantly drinks the water from the Lord’s feet shall always enjoy good health and will certainly attain union with Him (sāyujya).
The water from the Śālagrāma stone combined with Tulasī leaves shall be the pacifier of all diseases and the remover of all sins.
O best of sages, the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) offered in the presence of the Lord [yields the same].

It destroys the great sins (mahāpātaka) and bestows union with Viṣṇu. Furthermore, he who drinks the bathing water of the Lord, the enemy of Madhu, at the specific time of the ritual bath, shall attain all desires.
During a festival at a sacred ford (tīrtha), one should drink the water used for washing the feet;
it pacifies all the sins of men and bestows all prosperity.
Likewise, the water from the feet of the Preceptor (ācārya) and the water from the feet of one who is serene [should be drunk].
It is declared that the water from the feet is always a purifier and the destroyer of all sins.
Therefore, with every effort and with a state of pure devotion,
one should always drink the water from the feet of the Lord, His devotees, and the spiritual preceptor.

O best of the twice-born, he who takes even half a drop from the water of Hari’s abode and does not drink it should be known as an outcaste on this earth, even though he may be a Brahmin. He who makes himself invisible at this sacred ford [is likewise fallen].

O twice-born ones, there is no destruction of his sins even in a hundred lifetimes. However, he who bathes with devotion at the festival of the Tīrtha along with Cakrin shall obtain merit equal to bathing during a thousand eclipses. || 55-56 ||
If one who is devoid of faith should cast a *haritīrdha* onto the ground during its formal acceptance, he shall experience great suffering. However,
one should receive the *haritīrdha* with the hand of the officiating priest (*arcaka*).
O best of the twice-born, if this were not known as Surāsama, that would be a true holy place (tīrtha).
Or rather, O foremost of the twice-born, I shall describe specifically the fruit of beholding the Lord and of serving Him; listen with focused attention.
To him who goes daily to the temple of the God of gods,
Puruṣottama grants all his desires.
At the time of the festival of awakening, the sight of Viṣṇu is most excellent.
It pacifies all sins and increases longevity and health. On the eleventh lunar day, on the new moon, and on all festive occasions,
the sight of Śārṅgin (Viṣṇu) is purifying, meritorious, and the bestower of desired fruits.
O best of the twice-born, on the Ekādaśī known as Vaikuṇṭhapadā, when the Lord,
the enemy of Madhu, proceeds to the northern gate,
a vision of Him is difficult for all people to obtain and bestows liberation.
Whoever beholds the Lord seated upon His chariot attains,
with absolute certainty, the stainless state of being free from rebirth;
indeed, service to Viṣṇu mounted upon Garuḍa bestows the fruit of liberation.
"Let the gift of the Blessed One proceed upon the earth during the great festival; it has been declared to be the cause for attaining incomparable fruits.
Whoever beholds the Lord of Gods at the time of this auspicious festival,"
All his sins are undoubtedly destroyed.
O twice-born ones, on the day of the festival of the flower-sacrifice of the Lord, the enemy of Madhu,
at its conclusion, there is a great festival described as a lovers' quarrel.
O best of sages, this vision of Hari accompanied by Śrī, Bhū, Nīla, and others is exceedingly difficult even for yogis to attain; this is certain.
Furthermore, the vision of the Lord’s form at the time of His special descent is [even more rare].
O twice-born ones, the sight of even a single lamp offered to the Kṛttikās is the cause for the fulfillment of one's birth, bestows the fruit of liberation,
grants the eightfold sovereign powers, and is certainly a means for attaining mokṣa.
But the mere sight of the temple of Hari, through the feeling of devotion to Him,
shall bring about all prosperity and destroy all sins. Indeed,
the sight of the abode of Hari wards off the influence of malevolent planets.
Whoever beholds the Gopura of the Lord of the World with great devotion,
his lineage shall flourish upon the earth as long as the moon and sun endure.
Beholding the Discus situated at the top of the Gopura destroys all sins.

Having smelled the tulasī from the feet of the Blessed One, all men shall become free from disease on this earth and attain the world of Viṣṇu. O best of wise men, [so too shall those who smell] the flowers and sandalwood that are the remains of Hari's worship.
May this be accepted with bowed heads by those on earth who desire the highest good.
By holding upon one's head the auspicious sprouts from the *pālikās* and other vessels offered to the Blessed One, a person becomes cleansed of sin in this world.
On the tenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Āśvina, a victory festival is celebrated;
one should hold unhusked grains joined with *śamī* leaves above [the head].
For him, there is certain victory in all undertakings.
The ash from the fire oblation situated in the house of a Śūdra bestows inauspiciousness.
Therefore, O Brahmins, all men on earth should wear it during the festival of the Purifier (Pavitrotsava) of the active Vāsudeva. 79–80.

O twice-born ones, if one should constantly wear with devotion the sacred thread (pavitraka) offered for the sake of pacification, even if it has been discarded after worship, there shall be no deficiency in his ritual acts;
such is the firm conclusion of the scriptures.
And for those who, with devotion, have smelled the smoke of the burnt offerings in the house of Hari,
may there always be health, long life, prosperity, and an abundance of years;
may they possess the fortune of heroes and the fortune of enjoyments, as well as the saffron and other offerings presented there.
He by whom this is always maintained certainly attains good fortune;
he who beholds the Lord at the time of the *nirāñjana* [rite] shall become a man cleansed of sin and obtain great sovereignty. (84)
If a person eats barley for three days in sacred fields such as Svayambhū and others,
the multitude of his sins perishes instantly;
likewise, he who casts off his own body with devotion in meritorious fields [attains liberation].
For such a person, freedom from rebirth becomes a certain and eternal certainty.
Whoever worships the Lord of Gods with the thirty-two services, or even with the sixteen services, their desired goals shall be accomplished.
He who himself worships Hari with devotion by means of the Thousand Names on the eleventh lunar day, on a new moon day, or under the asterism Śravaṇa— on other festival days as well—
for him liberation is certain.
Whoever always worships the Lord of the World with one hundred and eight names, for him there shall always be great happiness. Or likewise, with twenty-four or twelve names.
Whoever performs worship for him, his bondage to worldly existence (bhava-bandha) is destroyed.

Furthermore, he who, for the pleasure of Hari, gives away cows, land, gold, wealth, and so forth, as well as grain, vehicles, and the like—elephants, horses, camels, and so on—[attains liberation]. 91–92.

O best of gods, one should devotedly offer alms-bowls and other items, ornaments, perfumes, flowers, fruits and the like, umbrellas, chowries, garments, and male and female servants; thereby, one shall obtain all that is desired.
O twice-born ones, for him who with devotion makes a gift of land on earth that endures forever, there shall be great happiness and an increase in lifespan;
likewise, through gifts of Sālagrāma stones and the like, as well as garments, ornaments, wealth, and so forth. (94–95)

He who pleases the priest in the presence of Vāsudeva shall become free from rebirth and highly renowned upon the surface of the earth. It is said that the fruitfulness of one's birth lies in sweeping the temple of Viṣṇu.

By holding chowries, fly-whisks, and the like, one shall attain residence in the heavenly world. By carrying an umbrella, a staff, and so forth, a person obtains his desired goals; it is taught that by directly carrying [the vehicle] for the Lord, one attains union with Viṣṇu.
The offering of flowers, garlands, and canopies yields the tenth fruit;

by means of temples and through dance, song, and so forth, a person obtains the fulfillment of their desires. By making the sound of musical instruments and the like, there will certainly be pleasure for Hari.
By reciting hymns and other praises of Viṣṇu, one shall attain union with Him (sāyujya).
By performing the purification of the site and other rites, one gains fame that cannot be pierced even by the piercing of a hundred vessels.
Furthermore, by lighting lamps, one obtains an auspicious state for bathing during planetary transits.
By the offering of articles worthy of daily worship,
the sin committed during seven lifetimes perishes instantly;
by the performance of a great festival, there is liberation from the five great sins.

During the festivals beginning with the Pavitra, for the Lord of the worlds, there is an increase of one's lineage and one attains union [with Him]; of this there is no doubt. This applies to the performance of the thousand-pitcher bath for the Enemy of Madhu.
One who has bathed at a thousand sacred fords shall certainly become a performer of sacrifices;
furthermore, the decoration of the village or even the decoration of the temple performed with great devotion during times of great festivals and the like [yields great merit]. (105)

May she be the accomplisher of all goals and the bestower of all prosperity. Through the act of cooking the oblation, may she grant the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. O Brahmins, what need is there for further elaboration? All duties belong to the Lord of the Universe.

It is declared that these grant special fruits; this is a certainty of truth. O King, he who builds a temple for Hari with devotion for the prosperity of his kingdom shall certainly attain union (sāyujya) with Viṣṇu.
If anyone constructs a pavilion on the ground, his lineage shall flourish until the dissolution of all beings;
this is likewise true for the construction of a gateway (gopura) and the installation of its pinnacle (śikhara). || 109-110 ||

O best of sages, one obtains the fruit of the sixfold lineage from that very moment upon the construction of a wall or a gate in the temple of Hari; indeed, the liberation from the bondage of saṃsāra is certain.
The installation of the emblem of heroism (vīra-lakṣmī) bestows great sovereignty;
the consecration of the flagstaff brings about all prosperity, and through it, the attainment of union with Hari (sāyujya) may occur upon this earth. || 112-113 ||
O best of sages, by constructing vehicles and other such items for the Lord, the Enemy of Madhu, one certainly attains the fruit of a hundred sacrifices. Furthermore,
O twice-born ones, having beheld the temple of the Blessed One, one should prostrate with all eight limbs.
Likewise, for the sight of the gopura and its spire,
as well as for the discus situated at the top of the spire and the tip of the banner, O King, [the merit is] the same.
One should perform a prostration on the ground like a staff with all eight limbs;
for whoever does so in this world, there shall be great fruit for them.
[This should be done] at the altar of offerings, at the doorway, and in the middle of the great pavilion.
A wise man, endowed with devotion and faith, should constantly perform the eight-limbed prostration (sāṣṭāṅga-praṇāma) in temples according to the very method previously described;
he should stand facing Viṣṇu and never show his back to Him.
O best of the wise, one should never sleep in the house of Hari in the vīrāsana posture or other such positions; by doing so, a great sin would be incurred.
Therefore, in this world, one should always sleep with a mind bowed in devotion.
Those desiring their own welfare should never themselves hold an umbrella, a staff, or sandals in the presence of the Blessed One,
nor even within the temple of the Blessed One or on the ground near him. 120–121.
The voiding of feces and urine, the spitting of phlegm,
and bathing— these should be avoided as they cause the provocation of Bhava.
Let there be a great festival for the God of gods, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow.
O best of the twice-born, until the day of the festival at the holy ford, all festivals such as weddings and others should be avoided;
O Brahmins, whoever should perform them would incur sin upon this earth.
O best of the twice-born, if during the festival of Viṣṇu one performs the festival of another deity out of deluded intent, then that leads to the destruction of that village,
provided it occurs at the time of Viṣṇu’s festival or prior to it.
Whatever rites such as marriage and the like one might perform will all become fruitless.
However, during the great festival of Vāsudeva, the Lord of Śrī,
those men who hear the kettledrum at the time of the invocation of the deities [attain merit].
They should not go to a foreign land that is more than a yojana distant;
for if they do go out of delusion, they will surely become afflicted by disease upon the earth.
[This applies] from the day the banner is raised until the day it is lowered.
If one should go to another country or even to another village,
there would be the destruction of his fame and his life-force would be diminished upon the earth;
therefore, with every effort, one should avoid going outside.
He by whom a great festival is performed shall attain the fruit of the horse-sacrifice (aśvamedha). In whatever region that festival takes place, O twice-born ones,
there shall be abundant rain for all, and the king shall attain prosperity.
For him who beholds the Lord of Birds (Garuḍa) at the time of hoisting the banner, there shall always be auspiciousness;
of this there is no doubt.
Furthermore, that person who hears the kettledrum at the time of invoking the deities [attains prosperity].
Having obtained all desired things here, one shall attain Vaikuṇṭha at the end; thus,
at the time of transition, and every day at the break of dawn,
one should bow to Hari and worship Him according to the path prescribed in the scriptures.
Whatever merit a person obtains by worshipping for one year, a worshipper obtains all that merit in a single day. Scorpio is situated in the Sun; there is the sight of the Kṛttikā lamp. 135–136.
Hearing the sound of the bell in the abode of Hara— which bestows all desires upon men and destroys all sins—
even the planets presiding over Brahma depart quickly to a great distance and shall not return again.
Beholding the Blessed One on the eleventh day (Ekādaśī) destroys all sins. Ritual acts such as worship performed on that day are remembered as yielding a thousandfold fruit.
The vow of Ekādaśī is declared in the world to be the most excellent of all.

O lords of sages, on that day one should also avoid performing the śrāddha for the ancestors; however, those who perform this on the following day according to the path of the scriptures [attain the results]. 140. It is indeed a wish-fulfilling tree for devotees, bestowing the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.

On the ninth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Āśvina, the festival of Vīra-lakṣmī should be celebrated on the Sarvatobhadra [mandala], which brings happiness to all the world. For whoever performs this festival, his prosperity shall become steadfast.
For him who celebrates the festival of Lord Hari on the day of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s birth, his cattle, lands, and gold increase; of this there is no doubt.
In whatever land this festival of the Lord of the worlds is performed, [there too prosperity shall flourish].
In that specific region, there will be a great increase in cattle.
On the birth anniversaries of his devotees and on his own birthday as well,
one should celebrate a grand festival in the presence of the God of gods.
Thus, for whoever performs [this rite] on earth, an increase in lifespan is proclaimed,
beginning from the Jyeṣṭhā-abhiṣeka until the Vāsantika festival. O Blessed One, for him who performs it with devotion, [there is always prosperity].

Those who see the ancient temple of the Lord with a spirit of devotion will undoubtedly obtain long life, health, and good fortune. Furthermore, in that region, there shall certainly be an increase in prosperity for both the king and the kingdom. (147-148)
One who performs the extraction (uddhāra) on the ground shall attain union with Hara;
O lords of sages, he who recites the mantra of the Blessed One at dawn attains his desired goals in a short time.

One who beholds with true devotion the Lord of the World, seated upon the lotus of the disc, during the Flower Sacrifice (Puṣpayāga), attains the supreme goal. Likewise, the chanting of His names and the hearing of them on this earth [bring the same fruit]. 150–151.
O Brahmins, by standing in the midst of battle upon the ground and praying with devotion to Hari, one shall become the remover of all sins and the destroyer of all obstacles;
such a person swiftly attains victory— of this there is no doubt.
The celebrants of the festival of the God, as well as the preceptors, the officiating priests,
the class of attendants, and the spectators of Hari,
having attained union (sāyujya), rejoice eternally like those who are ever-liberated (nityamukta). || 153-154 ||
On the eighth, the fourteenth, the ninth, on Friday,
on the full moon day, and on the new moon day, during the worship of Vīra-lakṣmī with her thousand names, using turmeric powder and saffron—
There is an increase of wealth and grain, and the certain attainment of Vaikuṇṭha.
[One should recite] the twelve-syllable mantra of Vāsudeva, the six-syllable mantra of Viṣṇu,
and also the great eight-syllable mantra of the glorious Nārāyaṇa.
O lords of sages, the Śrīrāmatāraka, the Śrīmantra, the pure Pauruṣasūkta, the Śrīsūkta,
the hymns beginning with Bhūmi and Nīla, and the Gītās taught by Hari [should always be recited] on this earth. || 158 ||
O best of the wise, by reciting the Thousand Names of Viṣṇu according to one's ability every day,
and by meditating upon the Lord of the Universe after chanting and reading them,
one is liberated from all the bonds of worldly existence.
O twice-born ones, for him who recites daily with devotion the great mantra of Garuḍa, the poisons of serpents and the like shall become poisonless.
Whoever on earth constantly recites the Hanuman-mantra-king,
the entire host of planetary spirits is liberated merely by the sight of him.

In this world as well, for these [deities], there shall arise the attainment of their desired objects. When the summer season has arrived, by satisfying Hari with cool offerings such as curd-rice and other foods, a man shall become free from all sins. 161
He who gives molasses-water, curd-rice, fans, and so forth, along with umbrellas, sandals, sacrificial fees, and fruits to Vaiṣṇavas and others during the month of Vaiśākha for the pleasure of Hari—
liberation stands within his grasp.
He who gives Himalayan wool, blankets, couches,
and bodices to the Vaiṣṇavas shall likewise take refuge in Vaikuṇṭha;
moreover, that best of gods should always eat the food of the Vaiṣṇavas.
There will undoubtedly be the direct grace of Hari;
moreover, the greatness of the five purificatory rites (saṃskāras) is truly incomparable and certain.
Therefore, those desiring union (sāyujya) should wear [the marks] upon the surface of their bodies.
O twice-born ones, whenever one beholds in this world a most excellent Śrīvaiṣṇava brāhmaṇa who is devoted to the worship of Hari, one should prostrate before him with all eight limbs;
by saluting him, a person always obtains the desired fruits upon the earth.

O twice-born ones, by eating at the home of even a single Śrīvaiṣṇava twice-born man, one obtains the fruit of satisfying thousands of Brahmins; O twice-born ones, such a person gains a place on the earth. Furthermore, a Śrīvaiṣṇava who is pleased bestows a [divine] womb upon one on this earth.
One who follows [another's] dress, speech, and so forth through mere outward appearance will certainly go to hell.
On this earth, one should honor a Vaiṣṇava by the mere presence of the vertical mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra);
for wherever that vertical mark is seen in the world, [he is to be honored].
By performing prostration before him, a man becomes cleansed of sin;
association with a Śrīvaiṣṇava destroys even the most heinous crimes (mahāpātaka). Drinking the water from his feet is the cause for the end of rebirth.
The food remaining after being eaten by the Śrīvaiṣṇavas is remembered as bestowing liberation;
by the mere act of eating it, one attains sāyujya with Viṣṇu.
A person who is devoted to worshipping the feet of the teacher of the Śrīmad Bhāgavata [attains this]. 172–173.
With a mind deeply absorbed in meditation upon the lotus feet of the Śrī-Vaiṣṇavas,
and having performed the service pleasing to Hari, one shall attain Śrī-Vaikuntha.
Furthermore, at the very beginning of the vision of the Lord, there is the vision of Śrī and the other attendants.
The form of the deity should be that of a man, bestowing freedom from disease and the removal of planetary afflictions.
Therefore, first performing the auspicious viewing of the deity,
one should then gaze at it starting from the feet up to the face.
O lords of sages, this is ordained for the Vaiṣṇavas and must be kept secret:
prostrating with only one hand, performing only a single circumambulation,
and stepping over the shadow of the temple, the staff of the twice-born, or that of Śauri.
Having left the place of the flagstaff, one should perform the circumambulation of Hari’s abode;

these are declared to be the givers of auspiciousness, for this is the certainty stated in all the scriptures. Circumambulating the abode of Hari is said to be equivalent to circumambulating the entire earth.
O best of the wise, those who light a lamp daily for two or three times, or as much as they are able, in the house of Śrī Viṣṇu during the month of Kārtika,
will undoubtedly attain union with Śrī Hari. 180.

O twice-born ones, he who installs the Lord of Gods together with Śrī and the other deities in his home and worships Him every day according to the full extent of his means—his sins are all liberated; of this there is no doubt. (181)
O Brahmins, may that [temple] become the bestower of desired objects in this world;
for he who, out of anger, greed, or other motives, punishes the priest, all the merit previously acquired by him shall perish. (182-183)
That house in which there is no Vaiṣṇava who worships the Lord shall indeed be a cremation ground; of this there is no doubt on earth.
A Vaiṣṇava house is always [auspicious] due to the conch, the discus, and the vertical sectarian marks (ūrdhvapuṇḍra).

O best of sages, one should adorn it on the ground according to the procedure prescribed in the scriptures. However, food prepared by a non-Vaiṣṇava that has not been offered to the Lord leads to the destruction of one's lineage and results in rebirth in the Raurava hell.
"O God, all those on this earth who are your servants—
those excellent twice-born ones endowed with the five sacraments—
whoever shall behold you at the time of the deity's worship, [they shall be purified]. 187-188.
"Upon this earth, for one who is devoid of the *ūrdhvapuṇḍra*,
there shall be great sin and his worship shall become fruitless.
Thus was it spoken by Hari in the past to the Lotus-born One.

One should never reveal this to one who is not a devotee nor to one who is not a disciple. O best of the twice-born, that which has been declared to you is more secret than the secret; it was spoken to you in brief so that it might be understood in detail.
Even for one who is incapable of performing the remaining rites, there shall be neither uncertainty nor doubt;
by merely hearing this, a person becomes cleansed of sin.

Thus ends the fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Greatness of the Lord’s Sacred Fords, Grace, and so forth," in the *Śrīparapuruṣasaṃhitā*, which is the essence of the secret teachings of the *Śrīpañcarātra-āgama*.
"O Blessed One, best among those who practice self-restraint, foremost among those who know all dharmas!
May the worshippers in the temples of the gods be ever devoted to their worship. (1)
Therefore, what should be done on this earth as half of their assistance,
by means of which a decision may be made for the purpose of propitiating that [deity] at the proper time?
Servants and other materials should be obtained on earth for the worshipper.
O Lord, tell us all of that in detail.
O venerable Nāradas, listen, all you sages who are devoted to meditation upon Hari.

I shall declare the determination of the qualified candidates for residence in the abode of the Blessed One. If that mansion of Hari were established on the surface of the earth by all its attendants, with enjoyments, attachments, and eternal riches; (4-5)
For the sake of protecting these [deities],
the sacrificer, with a tranquil mind, should determine the presiding deity at the conclusion of the installation of the god,
having first ascertained the officiating priests and others according to the injunctions of the scriptures.
Having given the temple of the Blessed One to those [deities] for the sake of accomplishing its power,
one should appoint a single person as the authorized official for the purpose of providing assistance to it—
one who is a true Brahmin, of virtuous conduct, truthful, and deeply learned.
He was possessed by a fear of sin and was learned in many scriptures;
he was an expert in the ritual procedures of the Pañcarātra, a proponent of the Veda, and a knower of dharma.
He had no desire for the wives of others and was free from greed.
Endowed with the five refinements, speaking kindly, and following the way of compassion;
desiring the increase of his mother’s honor, he was the crest-jewel of great devotees,
born of a noble lineage, and an expert in the science of yoga.
A virtuous person is steadfast, endowed with wisdom, peaceful, possessed of forgiveness and fortitude;
they are skilled in discerning the true from the false, ever humble, and a man of good character.
Whether a student, a householder, a forest-dweller, or a mendicant ascetic—
"O best of the twice-born, may Dadhīcāri, endowed with these characteristics and free from malignant diseases,
always reside in the temple of the gods;
O bulls among sages, I shall now declare what must be done for him."
From the hour of Brahmā until the conclusion of the worship,
he should always remain in the presence of the Blessed One, remaining pure at all times.
For the sake of performing worship at the proper time, he should attend to all necessary materials and servants.
The protector of the law shall give [the surplus] to those who perform worship and to those who have completed their tasks;
he alone shall oversee all income and expenditure from the gods,
and he shall have it recorded daily by scribes.
In the determination of eligibility, the ascetic is declared the highest, the householder is remembered as the middle, and the student (brahmacārī) as the lowest.
For it is for the sake of seeing Śiva that the Lord’s wives come here.
And by constantly beholding [the sun] on earth with devotion, one becomes worthy of dwelling near the God;
he who has renounced all attachments is remembered as a true ascetic (yati). 19–20.
O Brahmin, even if one should become honored by the world at all times,
therein too he should be pure and averse to the wives and wealth of others;
whether a householder or a celibate student, he should be a performer of dharma on this earth.
But a son born of a twice-born man from a Śūdra woman can never become a lord of dharma;
for it is said that at times of worship, service to a Śūdra is not permitted.
Therefore, he who performs dharma on earth while accompanied by a Śūdra woman is likewise [excluded].
Since these temples are established for the purpose of propagating one's own doctrine,
therefore a Brahmin who adheres to another doctrine cannot be a protector of dharma.
When a patron has a temple constructed on earth for the sake of his own lineage...
For the sake of the prosperity of the king and the kingdom,
he should determine the performers of dharma according to the path prescribed in the scriptures and by means of the ritual for that weapon;
O wise ones, if he performs all this at any other time, it shall be fruitless.

O twice-born ones, one who is a detractor of another's doctrine by his own nature would become a detractor of other doctrines as well. Therefore, when he is appointed to the office of a Dharma-maker, the respect and other virtues held for that institution in the world will perish.
Therefore, one should indeed point out a Brāhmaṇa who is well-versed in his own doctrine;
for on this earth, one who is not a Brāhmaṇa is unworthy of reciting the Vedas and other scriptures.
Consequently, such a person reflects upon the worship prescribed by the sacred texts as being merely a burden.
Therefore, one gains no fruit whatsoever from its construction,
because the presiding deity of a temple is not a protector of Dharma.
Consequently, one should always worship him in the world with the sentiment of Hari.
Except for a single officiating brahmin, one is capable of punishing all the attendants;
yet, on this earth, the performer of dharma (the king) should be the protector of dharma, and the patron of the sacrifice should punish him [if he transgresses]. || 31-32 ||
Immediately after the construction of the Bhagavadgeha on earth,
other images were determined for worship, endowed with all auspicious characteristics;
and at that very time, the performer of dharma acted as the patron (yajamāna) upon the earth.

The procedure for the ordeal must be determined as being endowed with the characteristics previously mentioned. However, if the sacrificer, out of delusion, should determine [the ordeal] by means of a twice-born man who lacks all the aforementioned characteristics, or one who is unfit, then [the result is invalid]. 34–35.
O Brahmins, there will be the destruction of that temple and misfortune for the region;
likewise, there will be the destruction of the patron and the ruin of the officiating authority.
Wherever the previously mentioned determination of an unfit ruler occurs, [such calamities shall follow].
Having performed the propitiatory fire-sacrifices (śāntihoma) and other rites, and having consecrated the temple of the Lord with sprinkling, the patron,
having ascertained that the carpenter is a supreme upholder of dharma and endowed with the proper characteristics,
should have the work carried out for the sake of pleasing Hari.
When the wealth for the sake of the officiating priests is half of the sacrificer's total assets,
the patron may determine whether it shall be land or a monetary fee;
in this world, land is considered the best, while a monetary fee is recorded as the lowest.
Therefore, with every effort, one should cause it to be bestowed upon the earth.
This shall certainly become the end of the lineage on this earth;
or else, if the ascetic is firmly resolved, it shall reach the end of his disciples.
Wherever the patron desires the protection of dharma, he should appoint a presiding lord over that place— one who, though lacking the previously mentioned characteristics, is nonetheless capable; or,
having determined a priest by name for that office, he should install him in that position.

Then, by his command, he himself should perform the duties appropriate to him. Day after day, in the presence of the God of gods, the protector of dharma should recite all the accounts of income and expenditure with devotion and humility.
If, at that time, there should be any doubt or even some contradiction,
then all the sages and devotees are capable of questioning [him] in Mālaya.
Having thus performed that recitation, the performer of dharma should immediately thereafter—
For the pleasure of the Blessed One, having obtained the consent of the worshipper regarding that leaf,
he then summoned all the servants in the palace of Viṣṇu and showed it one by one to Śauri. 46–47.
Always remaining in the presence of Vāsudeva as a protector of dharma,
he should offer salutations in the morning and make this petition:
"O God of gods, O Mahāviṣṇu, on this day in your temple..."
"By your command, I shall investigate all matters.
O Lord, out of compassion, please grant me the authority to punish any among all your servants in whom a fault may be found. (49-50)
Having thus informed the Lord of Gods with offerings of flowers, garlands, and so forth,
the guardian of the temple shall be honored every day.
Furthermore, the Lord’s materials, ornaments, and other items shall be personally accounted for by him.
Having informed his servants, he should also show them their respective counts.
Thus, having first established this daily practice, the protector of that dharma should, from that time forward,
maintain all religious duties until the final dissolution of Hari.
And whenever any fault or the like should arise among the servants in the house of the Blessed One due to the neglect of the observance of dharma,
let the upholder of dharma himself suppress that [fault] and enjoy [the fruits] upon this earth.
If a person who performs religious duties should, on this earth, take away even the slightest property belonging to the Lord— whether out of greed, delusion, or for any other reason—
he shall enter the womb of a dog for hundreds of thousands of births.
He who sees [the Lord] in the house of a Śūdra shall go to the Raurava hell until the dissolution of all beings,
and in this world he shall encounter every kind of suffering.
But he who sees [Him] while dwelling in the presence of the Blessed One in the house of a Ṭhakkura—
Whosoever, out of a deluded vision, performs a religious rite or an act of worship for the sake of seeing women who have assembled even for half a day,
he brings about the destruction of his lineage and shall go to the Raurava hell.
It has been declared that the garments, ornaments,
and other offerings of the Lord of Śrī (Viṣṇu) are fit to be accepted by the officiating priest alone;
therefore, one who performs religious duties perishes by stealing them.
But because one who performs religious duties might, out of greed, delusion, or other such motives, employ his own sons or kinsmen as servants of Hari,
for that very reason, hell shall always befall him on this earth.
Dwelling in a temple, occupying the seat of honor, and residing in comfort—
