these strike down the patron and the presiding priest on this earth.
Furthermore, [one must avoid] using the patron's name during daily and regular worship and other rites.
One should not cook [the offering] in a great field (mahākṣetra) that is auspicious, such as one where [the Buddha] manifested himself;
this worship should always be performed solely for the sake of protecting the world. Therefore, wherever the practitioner desires worship under his own name, [that is the place]. 64–65.
One should perform this worship individually and constantly;
at the conclusion of the festival,
one should always honor the sacrificer in the abode of Hari with flowers, garlands, ointments, and other offerings on this earth.

O twice-born ones, when the cause is not directly perceived, Dharmapālaka shall always be honored according to the previously mentioned rule for the attainment of that result; however, wherever on earth the sacrificer is a non-Brāhmaṇa, [he shall be honored]. 67–68.

O lords of sages, one should first tie the protective thread (rakṣāsūtra) to the bell during the *tutadhsāna* rite; thereafter, one should tie a single worldly [thread] to the patron (*yajamāna*). All the garments and other items for the initiation (*dīkṣā*) should likewise be prepared in that same manner.
This is the procedure for the determination and other regulations concerning Dharmapāla.
Thus ends the fifth chapter, titled "The Procedure for Determining the Authority of Dharma," in the *Śrīparamapuruṣasaṃhitā*, which is the essence of the secrets of the *Śrīpañcarātrāgama*.
[Then the] Sages [spoke].

O Blessed One, tiger among sages, skilled in the essence of all scriptures, for what purpose should one perform the ritual sprinkling (saṃprokṣaṇa) in the house of Hari? O Lord, what is said regarding this distinction here? Please explain it in detail.
Śrī Nārada said:
"Listen, all you sages, with minds endowed with devotion;
today I shall describe in detail the procedure for the ritual sprinkling (saṃprokṣaṇa)."
The sprinkling of the temple, the removal of the food of the enemy of Madhu (Viṣṇu),
the peace-offering (śāntihoma), and the gift of food— these are declared to be the methods of purification (saṃprokṣaṇa).
O lords of sages, [this applies] when the temple falls or even when it shakes.
When the flagstaff or other parts are severed, when the pinnacle is destroyed,
when the image itself falls or shakes, as well as when it laughs; likewise,
upon the omission of worship, the destruction by fire, or the occurrence of fractures in its limbs.
When the food offering (naivedya) is missing, or when the unbroken lamp is extinguished,
and likewise when fire or other damage occurs to the temple, the banner, or the image;
and also in cases such as the restoration of what is dilapidated— sprinkling (saṃprokṣaṇa) is declared [as the remedy].
In the event of earthquakes, excessive rain, lightning strikes, or scant rainfall;
during regional calamities or ill omens—one should perform the ritual sprinkling (saṃprokṣaṇa).
[This applies to] umbrellas, chowries, garments, and so forth, as well as musical instruments, vehicles, and ornaments.
O Brahmins, if it should burn, one should perform propitiatory oblations and other rites;
O dwellers of the earth, if the image should be touched by worms, insects, and the like, or if rainwater should fall upon the idol during its consecration; || 9-10 ||

One should perform the sprinkling, the bathing, and the propitiatory fire-offering (śāntihoma). If the image has been touched by a Brahmin who does not perform worship, or if it has been touched by hair, body hair, and the like, as well as by spit and other such impurities; || 11 ||
One should perform a ritual sprinkling (saṃprokṣaṇa) with vultures, crows, monkeys, dogs, and the like, according to the prescriptions of the scriptures. Likewise,
[this applies] when entering a temple in the company of outcasts (caṇḍāla), dogs, and so forth.
If non-Aryans or common men enter the inner sanctum (garbhagṛha),
or if washermen or water-carriers enter the intermediate space,
or if crows, serpents, and the like enter the inner sanctum; || 14 ||
O best of the twice-born,

if the appearance of menses should occur among women in the temple, or if there is a miscarriage or a birth, then one should perform the ritual sprinkling (saṃprokṣaṇa) according to the prescribed rules. || 15-16 ||
When those affected by impurity due to birth or other causes enter the temple,

one should then perform a ritual sprinkling (saṃprokṣaṇa) according to the very path prescribed in the Śāstras. O Brahmins, if the image has been touched by adulterers, thieves, or the like, [one must likewise act].
If birth and death should occur within the temple precincts,
or when those who have committed sins bring honey, meat, and the like into the temple,
then one should perform a complete sprinkling ritual (saṃprokṣaṇa) and have a peace-offering (śāntihoma) performed for all.
O best of sages, when the immortal body has been brought to the house of the Lord, one should immediately cast it far away and perform all the rites,
such as the sprinkling of water, according to the prescribed injunctions.
Just as the touch of heat may occur upon the body of the Blessed One,
so too when the touch of fireflies and the like occurs upon the image,
then one should perform sprinkling, bathing, and the propitiatory fire-offering (śānti-homa).
Wherever the worship of the Enemy of Madhu (Viṣṇu) is performed with flowers and other materials that are forbidden or defiled—
such as when it is contaminated by worms, insects, stones, hair, or body hair— there a ritual sprinkling (saṃprokṣaṇa) must take place.
One should offer food to Hari; that is known as *saṃprokṣaṇa*.
If, during the time of pilgrimage, one should have a vision of another deity, at that time one should perform *saṃprokṣaṇa* for Vāsudeva.
In the event of the omission of the daily festival or the neglect of the daily worship,
one should immediately perform an ablution and carry out a propitiatory fire-offering (śāntihoma).
Then, one should once again perform all the rites, beginning with worship, according to the prescribed rules.
O best of sages, for those who perform the special bathing and all other rites such as the peace-offering (śāntihoma) when there is an omission of the daily food offering (nityanaivedya),
if the omission of the food offering for the Slayer of Madhu should occur for three days, [the following must be done].
Then one should perform the ceremonial bath with one hundred and eight jars;
likewise, one should duly perform the propitiatory fire-offerings (śāntihoma) and other rites,
beginning for three days and continuing until the end of the fortnight.
If the offering of food (naivedya) should be omitted for any reason whatsoever,
one should perform the bathing and other rites according to the most excellent method;
this should be done for a month or even longer if the naivedya has been omitted.

The bathing of the Lord who wields the Śārṅga bow with a thousand jars is prescribed. O best of wise men, if there is an excess of wind for six months, or if the food offering (naivedya) is omitted, then a re-consecration must be performed according to the rules.
In the event of the omission of the great festival, or even upon the lapse of the prescribed time,
one should perform the sprinkling and other rites and then conduct the great festival once again. Likewise,
when the fire has been extinguished, or when the sacrificial fire is absent, or when an inauspicious sight is perceived.
O lords of sages, if there should be a defect in the sacrificial ladle,
or if there should be a defect such as the fuel being too moist, or likewise if there should be a defect in the ghee, such that offerings like the *homa* must be performed with water; || 34-35 ||
Then, O best of the wise, one should perform the sprinkling and the peace-offering (śānti-homa) according to the prescribed rite. If the flagstaff is destroyed during the midst of the great festival,
one should perform the peace-offering and other rites, and then hoist another flagstaff.
O twice-born ones, when sprouts do not emerge from the seed-vessels and so forth,
or if those sprouts wither away according to the prescribed rule,
one should perform a sprinkling with water over the fire and complete the rite of pacification (śānti). || 37-38 ||
Furthermore, one should replant the seedlings according to the prescriptions of the scriptures.
However, when the kusha grass, the sacrificial brush (kūrca), the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), the altar (āla),
and the ritual implements perish or are consumed by fire, then one should perform the ritual sprinkling (saṃprokṣaṇa).
Having again consecrated those [vessels] as before, one should deposit them as previously done.
Having performed the Brahmakūrca rite preceded by the peace-offering (śāntihoma) and other rites,
one should once more install [the deity] and complete the remainder of the ritual.
O best of sages, if the door-arches or the water-pots (kumbhas) are destroyed or burnt,
one who performs the ritual sprinkling (saṃprokṣaṇa) according to the scriptures [must act];
likewise if a cat, a mouse, a lizard, or a scorpion [should enter].
O great lord of sages, when snakes and other creatures fall into the sacrificial fire-pit,
one should then perform the sprinkling rite (saṃprokṣaṇa) and the pacifying oblation (śānti-homa) according to the prescribed rule.
This should be done wherever a nest containing honey or an anthill may have arisen within the altar.
Having sent them far away from here, one should perform a peace-offering (śāntihoma).
If the birth or death of cats, mice,
and other such creatures occurs within the temple, sprinkling with water (prokṣaṇa) is prescribed by the sages.
When a cat, a mouse, a snake, a scorpion, a mongoose,
a firefly, a crow, a vulture, a donkey, a dog,
or a cock enters the house, or when there is the discharge of feces, spittle, and so forth; || 46-47 ||
O lords of sages, whether one performs [the rite] in the temple, or even upon the image itself—
if an image has been consecrated by them, then that is known as *saṃprokṣaṇa*. It is prescribed for all forms of worship, both daily (*nitya*) and occasional (*naimittika*), and for all festivals.

Where an action has passed its proper time, one should perform a propitiatory oblation (śāntihoma). O best of sages, it is certain that the omission of ritual materials destroys the donor, while the omission of mantras destroys the officiating priest; indeed, all ritual components [must be complete].
If there should be any omission or similar lapse regarding the Pavitra and other festivals,
one should indeed perform a ritual sprinkling (saṃprokṣaṇa) and then carry out all those rites for the gods.
O Brahmins, [one should likewise attend to] the vessels for the Arghya and Pādya offerings, as well as the hand-bell.
If it falls upon the ground, there should be a light sprinkling with water.
During the festivals of the year, whenever there is a breakage or similar incident,
one should perform sprinkling and other rites after observing whether the damage was slight or great.
If the nīrāñjana performed with water from a jar and kāleya incense destroys the luster of Hari,
one should perform the nīrāñjana after bathing the Lord with flowers and water.
But at the time of the daily worship, if there is a deficiency in garlands, flowers, and so forth,
one should pray for forgiveness from Kṣhara and offer that [offering] twice over.
O wise ones, this is the proclamation of the rules regarding the sprinkling and other rites;
if anyone should fail to perform them out of greed, his own destruction will come to pass. The deity will become displeased, and that kingdom shall perish.
"O twice-born ones, the destruction of that *ālaya* (the abode of the mind) shall then occur very quickly.

(55) Thus ends the sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Observances such as Sprinkling," in the *Śrī Paramapuruṣa-saṃhitā*, which is the essence of the secret teachings of the *Śrī Pañcarātra-āgama*.
The Sages:
O Nārada, best among the twice-born and foremost of the sages,
please describe the nature of transgressions committed through both knowledge and ignorance within the temples of this world,
as well as the classification of those offenses.
"Speak to us, O Lord thick with compassion; tell us that power, O Master.
Śrī Nārada said:
"Now I shall describe in detail the determination of improper conduct (apacāra)."
O best of sages, O twice-born ones, for one who has committed an offense on earth in the presence of the Blessed One due to causes such as anger, greed,
or pride, there shall be neither enjoyment nor liberation in this world.
The contemplation of ordinary water at the bathing-place of the Lord’s feet,
and the contemplation of ordinary food through the grace of Vāsudeva;
smelling and even eating food prior to the offering of the *naivedya*.
O Brahmins, by eating the prasāda of Śauri, one attains purification of the hands;
O best of the twice-born, even during war with the enemies of the gods, or when using the sacrificial fire-pit, or when discharging urine,
feces, and the like, or spitting— [these acts do not cause impurity].
Dwelling in a temple, sleeping there, eating there,
and sitting on the foremost seat are recorded as great defects (mahādoṣa).
Regarding the consumption of the remnants of Viṣṇu's offerings (prasāda), one should maintain the realization that it transcends time and other such limitations.
Wearing the remains of offerings (nirmālya), showing disrespect toward the worship of the Lord,
longing for worldly favor, doubting the purity of Hari’s abode, and doubting the purity of those who dwell there—
by doing any of these things in this world, one's lineage shall perish.
Having gone from the temple to his home and performed the washing of his feet,
he [perceived] the nature of stone, metal, and so forth in the form of the Lord;
likewise, he perceived the nature of mockery in the festivals and other rites of the wielder of the Śārṅga bow.
When the Lord arrived uninvited at her house and the door-bolts were released,
she set about to honor him; yet, when the Lord was revealed to her sight,
she engaged in quarreling and spoke untruths in his presence.
On the surface of the earth, wearing the garments, ornaments, and other belongings of the Blessed One;
drinking liquor in a temple; eating meat and the like;
laughing at animals, birds, and so forth; and likewise sexual union with women—[these are forbidden]. 15.
Theft, mockery, and the speaking of words of censure—
whatever has been done by anyone is said to bring about the destruction of that person's lineage.
Likewise, the seizing of the Lord's property and the reviling of Hari [are likewise destructive].
O best of the twice-born, entering the inner sanctum even by one who is not an officiating priest (arcaka),
regarding a worshiper of the Blessed One as being no different from an ordinary Brahmin, and the reviling or punishing of the officiating priest— [these are grave offenses]. 17–18.
The life and prosperity of that deluded soul who inflicts suffering upon him or likewise seizes his property shall perish. Furthermore,
one who carries an umbrella or sandals, or carries a staff upon the ground [is likewise subject to this].
If one should enter the house of a devotee of Hara, the destruction of that person's lineage is ordained.
Furthermore, if one should obstruct with a parasol or footprints the path of a devotee of the God of gods,
he shall attain the dreadful Raurava hell.
O twice-born ones, whoever should take away the flowers and other offerings brought for the worship of the Blessed One Viṣṇu shall attain the most terrible hell. Furthermore,
one wearing a bodice and a turban must not enter the temple of Hari.
Nothing should be shown to the God of gods, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, without being asked.
He who abandons the holy place of Hari due to a lapse in devotion shall suffer the destruction of his lineage and will certainly go to hell.
By visiting sacred fords and other such places, or by performing sacrifices to Viṣṇu and so forth,

the life and prosperity of one who causes [the deity] to fall upon the ground shall perish. Furthermore, he who, though not dull-witted, considers himself a practitioner of ritual action and is possessed by egoism— [his merit is lost].
If one abandons the sacred ford of Hari out of fear at all times, all the merit previously acquired by him perishes;
furthermore, he is considered unworthy to enter a temple of the gods. || 26-27 ||
Upon entering the abode of Mlecchas, Pāṣaṇḍas,
and other such castes, as well as those who are not devotees, one's own dignity is utterly destroyed;
therefore, their unfitness for entry has been established.
When that entry occurred for whatever reason,
he performed a great consecration (saṃprokṣaṇa) and offered the Śāntihoma sacrifice;
meanwhile, the three women had arrived for the purpose of beholding the Blessed One.
He indeed brings about the existence of another; his destruction will come at the time of the Lord of Śrī’s favor being employed [for another purpose].
On this earth, one should always avoid conversing with others and similar activities.
Transgressing [the rules of] faith, striking [the image], reviling it four times,
defiling it by any means whatsoever— these are causes for the destruction of one's lineage; as are saluting with only one hand and performing only a single circumambulation.
Those on earth who desire their own welfare should always avoid entering the temple of Hari; likewise,
one should avoid deriding the temple of the Lord or the proclamation of the superiority of other deities,
as well as the sight of the vertical *puṇḍra* marks and so forth, if such acts are performed in jest.
For one who censures the hearing of discourses on the life of the Blessed One and so forth, great suffering will arise in whatever land they may be;
likewise, for one who creates obstacles during the construction of a temple, [the same shall occur]. (35–36)
Without a doubt, his lineage shall perish before long;
he who brings about the destruction of a great festival on this earth, having become afflicted with jaundice, shall go to hell. (37)

O best of gods, he who extinguishes the fire in the sacrificial pit or the flame of a lamp in a temple shall suffer terrible misery on this earth; so too for one who defiles or reviles devotees. || 38-39 ||
And the destruction of all that is desired shall surely occur upon this earth for one who enters the temple after consuming honey, meat, and the like,
while remaining unwashed, impure, and devoid of the vertical *ūrdhvapuṇḍra* mark. (40)
O best of sages, his lineage shall surely come to an end;
for at the time of the pilgrimage, having seen the Lord of Gods nearby in his own chariot,
no one on earth will find satisfaction with offerings and other gifts.
All his grains, wealth, and other possessions shall become fruitless for him—
that man who, upon seeing Hari arrived in the midst of the city,
makes himself invisible and does not offer a salutation.
He shall experience great suffering and go to the Raurava hell.
Furthermore, he who gives fruits and the like that are remnants of another's meal,
or scents, flowers, and so forth that have been smelled by others, incurs the sin of Hari.

O lords of sages, he who would burn a temple or even the house of a priest will very swiftly meet the destruction of his lineage; of this there is no doubt. He who would harbor improper passion toward the wives of the priest—
For him, there shall be exceedingly great and terrible suffering upon the surface of the earth (47).
He who looks with derision upon Brahmins who are great devotees of the Lord—
his previously acquired merit and even his wealth shall perish (48).
If one should drive away the draft animals of the chariot belonging to Jagannātha while standing upon it,
he shall experience great suffering as he constantly falls to the ground.
Whatever dharma scripture belongs to the temple of the gods is the Pāñcarātrika.
Know that for the man who harbors doubt regarding that authorless nature [of the scripture], there shall be the destruction of his lineage; this is determined by all the scriptures.
[This applies] from the commencement of the chariot ascent until the festival day of the sacred ford.
Going to another village or elsewhere brings destruction to anyone [who does so].
When a festival for the gods is underway, one should not perform a festival for humans.
For that deluded soul who does so, the extinction of his lineage is certain.

He who enters the temple during a period of impurity caused by death shall suffer the destruction of his lineage and be reborn in the Raurava hell. Furthermore, he who enters the temple of Śauri while naked [shall likewise suffer]. || 53-54 ||
One who is burdened with the great sins (mahāpātaka) becomes a Caṇḍāla on this earth;
he should go before the house of a Brāhmaṇa by the path of the footprints.
At the front part of the temple, he should perform a salutation.
To act otherwise is said to be the destruction of one's family (56).
The misappropriation of the property of the gods is declared a great sin (mahāpātaka); likewise is the devising of obstacles against the servants of the Lord (57).
O brāhmaṇas, whatever fruit, flower, grain, or other such things are said to be causes for the destruction of one's lineage,
one should offer that which is fresh to Śrī Hari.
O son of Śauri, whatever one might give from that source, no increase thereof shall occur on earth.
In other matters, however, one should obey the command of the officiant (arcaka),
whether he be the master of the shrine or one endowed with devotion, faith, and so forth.

"Whoever does not act in this way shall experience great suffering. O best of the twice-born, thus should the description of improper conduct within the house of the Blessed One be understood by all in this world who desire their own welfare.
Thus ends the seventh chapter, titled "The Description of Offenses against the Lord," in the Śrī Paramapuruṣa Saṃhitā, which is the essence of the secrets of the Śrī Pāñcarātra Āgama.
The Sages said:
O Blessed One, O tiger among sages, you who are ever devoted to Hari!
Previously, you described all the characteristics of one who has sought refuge;
however, today we wish to hear about his extraordinary disposition.
By what great disposition do all people in the world always [behave]?
O great sage, those who are immersed in the ocean of worldly existence are worthy of attaining union with the Lord of Śrī, even as if they were not immersed;
listen, all you sages, out of a desire for the grace of the world.
O best of beings, that which you desire to hear today—

namely, the single process of meditative cultivation (bhāvanākrama) considered most preeminent in the world— in whatever action one engages, whatever state of being exists therein will certainly become manifest.

Those people in the world who, due to causes such as the omission of ancillary rites while performing service to Hari, or because of poverty while constructing temples and other edifices, continue their practice with that same disposition; [they attain the goal].
Those men who are always devoted to pilgrimages to sacred fields and likewise always well-bathed in meritorious waters attain the supreme, great, and difficult-to-attain abode of Hari.
O lords of sages, whether one is a builder of Hari’s temple, intent on sacrificial rites on earth,
or otherwise devoid of that disposition and conducts oneself with a different state of mind,
they shall possess no power whatsoever from those acts.
Like the bathing of an elephant, all their actions are fruitless.
Today, O high-minded one, I shall declare to you the characteristic of contemplation for one who has sought refuge,
which he performs upon this earth.
O best of sages, the certainty regarding that very Viṣṇu— namely, the attainment of union (sāyujya)—

was previously declared by me in the section on the procedure for the worship of Hari. [This applies] to the construction of temples and the like, as well as to the consumption of consecrated food (prasāda) and so forth.

Likewise, regarding the practice of dharma and other virtues as taught in all the scriptures, I shall today explain to you in detail that state of being through which one should proceed— the sequence of meditative cultivation for devotees who are incapable [of the higher paths].
O lords of sages, listen to that which one who has taken refuge attains in this world through all common activities—
eating, bathing, drinking, and so forth— all of which yield great fruit.
A householder should always regard his own home as the temple of Hari;
thinking, "I am the worshipper, my wife and sons are other attendants," he should conduct himself thus within the house of Hari. (16-17)
One always obtains merit that is honored; of this there is no doubt.
While engaged in the nourishment and adornment of one's own wife and children, one should always meditate upon Śauri, who dwells within them.
Having understood that all this has been offered upon the lower petal,
that best of men obtains the merit offered to Hara;
he who maintains a true disposition toward the washing of his own body [attains this].
O wise ones, sweeping and other such services in the temple of the Blessed One;
wearing one's own clothes and ornaments in the house of Hari;
and the offering of food after having first entered one's own home—[these are forbidden].

Thus, by the mere thought [of this], the foremost of all sages always obtains all that power; there is no doubt about this on earth. By the salutation of the Vaiṣṇavas and others, that which resides in their hearts [is attained].
Having meditated upon Śrī Hari with the mind, one obtains the fruit of that meditation;
likewise, in the performance of the twilight rites (saṃdhyā) and so forth, as well as in the libations to the gods, sages, and ancestors,
[one attains success] through mere devotion alone to Him who is the embodiment of all the gods.
O best of sages, Hari is truly propitiated on this earth by one who makes a firm resolve; O brahmins,
whatever garment or ornament may have been dropped or lost on the surface of the ground by anyone at all through negligence— [he who restores it gains the same merit].

By the mental disposition of offering all things, such as clothing and the like, to Hari, one obtains everything pertaining to that [divine] state; of this there is no doubt on earth. Even if his wealth and other possessions have been stolen by a thief—
One should contemplate that all of this is offered to Śrī Mahāviṣṇu.
O best of sages, by means of that great disposition, Śauri, residing within the heart of the thief, is satisfied with the aforementioned food and other offerings. 28–29.
The Lord of Gods should consider himself pleased with that very person in whose world, upon this earth, great suffering shall arise; however,
he should be pleased with him on this earth in whom Mahāviṣṇu is pleased.
All that has been commenced, which has afflicted [us] through birth after birth,
shall indeed today, at the end of your devotion, lead to sāyujya with Hari.
Therefore, in this world, for devotees, the occurrence of suffering [is only for a time].
What is the use of men on this earth having an abundance of wealth?
Only an increase in the bonds of worldly existence will come to pass.
Therefore, Hari alone desires to grant liberation through union (sāyujya) to him [who possesses it].
Having previously endured great sufferings, he himself purified [the world];
for the sake of creation, the God of gods is considered equal in both pleasure and pain.
Therefore, one who has taken refuge [in Him] maintains an even-minded disposition toward both happiness and sorrow.
Having gained the grace of Hari, one should contemplate the origin of suffering in this world,
wherein for some there is excessive wealth,
happiness, wives, and sons, yet along with infamy and lack of respect.
His devotion to the Blessed Lord shall always be but slight.
Therefore, even one who is deeply afflicted here on this earth,
if he has taken refuge and is constantly intent upon meditation on the feet of Hari, shall attain liberation.
For in this world, death arises for all beings through the body;
however, no one is able to know even its mere arrival.
Therefore, one should take refuge in one's own self, which stands within the fangs of death.
Having understood that all things are always non-existent in reality, and desiring freedom from rebirth,
one should conduct oneself in all affairs while meditating on Mādhava within the heart. Furthermore,
if one should go near the house of a thief, even along the path, [one should remain mindful].
Even one who has not bathed and is impure, having entered the temple,
may behold the Blessed One with devotion and a pure mind. That best of men who remembers Hari within his own heart with a spirit of service—
May he become completely pure and stainless in this world.
Therefore, whenever one should obtain the vision of any devotee by chance,
one should practice that vision even if devoid of external purity.
Furthermore, the sight of Śauri will itself effect one's purification;
by His own majesty alone, He will consume the entire category of great sins (mahāpātaka).
That power which is difficult to attain on earth through bathing, giving, recitation, and other such acts—[He shall bestow it]. 45.
All that he shall obtain on this earth through service to Hari.
In this world, the body of whomever it may be is but a bubble;
all people in this world always stand within the jaws of death.
Therefore, that fool who, out of delusion, abandons the true blessing of the vision of Śrī Hari— which is accomplished without effort— on account of impurity and other such reasons,
Furthermore, one may not find the appropriate time on this earth to perform [these rites].
Therefore, having taken refuge [in the Lord], one should always regard the vision of the Blessed One and so forth as being of supreme importance,
and seek them wherever they may be found.
O Brahmins, whenever one performs any other duty or any other task in this world by making the service of Hari the primary focus,
it is according to the command of the Blessed Lord.
Therefore, knowing this, O Lord of the world, you should indeed act;
for when He is always satisfied with them, all desired things are granted.
And he who performs meritorious deeds on earth with desire [shall likewise attain his goal]. 52–53.
Even for him, the Lord of Śrī indeed grants only those fruits that he himself desires;
when one afflicted by intense fever prattles about food and such things,
so too one afflicted by the fever of worldly existence desires all manner of objects of desire.
Just as food is given to a mother upon seeing her first pregnancy,
so too is the desired object given to Hari upon beholding Him for the second time;
therefore, virtuous people should always abandon actions performed with selfish desire.
However, one who has taken refuge [in Him], perceiving everything as dependent on Hari and having surrendered all burdens to the Lord of Śrī, may move about upon the earth;
for him, no fault or the like shall arise in any undertaking whatsoever.
O Brahmins, if one always gazes with a serene mind upon the power of the directions,
having gone to all the divine sacred fields and other such places, one beholds Janārdana residing there, endowed with infinite majesty and other qualities. (58–59)
By beholding the specific divine sports (līlā) of Śrī Hari and so forth, and by not seeing anything else,
one attains the bliss of Brahman at the end and achieves union (sāyujya) with Hari.
O twice-born ones, now hear about the superiority of the divine sacred fields (divyakṣetra) and other such places.
At the conclusion of the installation of the deity, the preceptor,

having established the power of his own asceticism and his creative energy within his own body, shall cause the deity to be fixed upon the earth through the aperture of Brahma by the touch of his own hand.

From that time forward, those great devotees who had taken refuge and were masters of self-restraint, desiring to show grace to the worlds, entered his physical form through the mere power of their own asceticism and by means of pure devotion alone. 63.
Therefore, those divine places where gods, sages, and others reside are proclaimed;
they are named after the sacred fields and are treasuries of the power of penance for true devotees.
By the mere sight of them, one is liberated from all sins.
Dwelling in sacred fields and the relinquishing of one's own body are said to be solely the causes for attaining a good rebirth; likewise,
wearing the remains of offerings (nirmālya) and so forth from Śauri, the Lord of those sacred fields.

There, on the surface of the earth, the consumption of the prasāda and other offerings at the sacred ford (tīrtha) is the pacifier of all sins, the bestower of all happiness, the cause of freedom from disease,
and the means for attaining longevity and prosperity.
O best of sages,
let there be no doubt that those who are devoted in sacred fields will always be like gods;
indeed, they attain a special greatness upon the surface of the earth.
Therefore, their company and the sight of them yield great fruit;
one will certainly obtain the increase of longevity and health, as well as the perfection of knowledge.
Furthermore, whoever should give them cows, land, clothing, wealth, and so forth—
O best of sages, may this [act] certainly yield a thousandfold fruit.
By feeding even a single Vaiṣṇava twice-born who dwells in that sacred field,
one obtains on this earth the fruit of satisfying a thousand Brahmins.
Formerly, the Lotus-seated Lord himself heard all of this from Hari and,
out of affection for me, revealed it to me.
That same supreme secret has now been explained to you.

Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "The Description of the Distinctive Nature of Devotion," in the Śrī Paramapuruṣasaṃhitā, which is the essence of the secrets of the Śrī Pañcarātra Āgama. The Sages said:
O Blessed One, O tiger among sages, O bestower of auspiciousness upon the world!

O highly fortunate one, if you have compassion for us, please tell us the determination of the rules regarding the Śrī Jayantī festival and other such observances, as they have been declared by the sages. Thus spoke Śrī Nārada.
Listen, O best of the Naimiṣa sages, as you all observe this:
the determination of festivals and other rites will now be concluded. [This is] Śrī Rāmanavamī.
In the month of Caitra, during the dark fortnight, on the ninth day under the asterism Punarvasu,
when the sun was entering Aries at midday while it was Cancer [in the zodiac],
Hari himself, the Lord of the Universe, appeared as Rāmacandra.
Therefore, O Brahmins, [the day] joined with Punarvasu, or even not joined with it,
occurring at the time of the Sun's entry into Aries,
whether joined with the eighth lunar day of the bright fortnight of Caitra or even devoid of it by a single digit— [that is the proper time].
Or even on the ninth day joined with the Parva-vedha, as was done previously;
having thus determined, he then sat before Tārāma, the Lord of the World,
with auspicious offerings such as oblations, festivals, ritual bathing, worship, and enjoyments.

O lords of sages, for the sake of the welfare of the world, one should satisfy [the deity] every year on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Vaiśākha, which is indeed the auspicious festival of Nṛsiṃha (Śrīnṛsiṃhajayantī).
Setting aside the *pūrva-vedha* (prior penetration) and other such [faults], even if joined with the *para-vedha* (subsequent penetration),
one should observe the pure fourteenth day— or even a single *muhūrta* or a fraction of it—
and on that very day, one should properly worship Śauri Nṛhari.
That [day] is renowned as Jayantī, belonging to Nṛsiṃha, the Lord of the Universe.
By gratifying the Lord of the World with offerings of curd-rice, jaggery-rice, and other such cool foods,
men shall always obtain happiness and well-being in this world.
One should perform the special ablutions and preliminary rites according to the scriptures.
If a man, out of delusion, observes the fourteenth day when it is pierced by [the conjunction with] Kāma, he shall be deprived of his wealth; therefore, one should avoid it.
Likewise, one should avoid the day when the moon is conjoined with Svātī or joined with the constellation Vṛṣabha,
as well as the fourteenth day of the month of Madhu; [on these days] one should abandon the Śrī Kṛṣṇa Jayantī.
O best of the wise, I shall now declare the determination regarding the Janmāṣṭamī and Jayantī of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Teacher of the World,
for those among the Śrī Vaiṣṇavas who perform rites with specific desires on this earth. 14.14-15ab.
For them, the Janmāṣṭamī has been prescribed; for other great souls who are especially devoted to selfless action and are serene,
it is renowned as Śrī Jayantī, which bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
On the eighth lunar day of the month of Śrāvaṇa, during the night of the Rohiṇī constellation on a Monday,
Śauri, the son of Devakī, the illustrious Kṛṣṇa, was born.
Therefore, every year on this very day, one should worship Puruṣottama.

O best of the wise, one should gratify [the deity] with various offerings and diverse services, as well as with special festivals. This should be done on the first day of the month of Nabhas, or when the sun enters Leo.
O lords of self-restraint, one should perform the festival on the day of Siṃhabhadra.
One should avoid the eighth lunar day when it is joined with the seventh, as well as Rohiṇī when it is pierced by Kṛttikā. || 20-21 ||
O twice-born ones, even on a pure Aṣṭamī that is free from the piercing of the seventh lunar day,
if Rohiṇī is not present,
then one should indeed perform the great festival with [the moon] conjoined with Mṛgaśīrṣa on that same day.
O lords, if the eighth lunar day (Aṣṭamī) has already commenced before the star Rohiṇī,
one should abandon that defiled Aṣṭamī and arrange for the festival on the pure [following] day.
When both the eighth lunar day and Rohiṇī are defiled by conjunction (vedha) and other such factors, [one should proceed accordingly].
Then, one should perform the festival on the ninth day when it is joined with Mṛgaśīrṣa;
or, if on the ninth day Rohiṇī is defiled [by being conjoined with a malefic],
one should indeed perform that great festival on the tenth day when it is joined with Mṛgaśīrṣa.
If two lunar mansions (nakṣatras) should occur within a single Siṃha month, one should first abandon the former and perform the festival during the latter;
provided that the second nakṣatra is not defiled by the transit of the sun (saṃkrānti). || 26-27 ||
Therefore, first of all, the conjunction of the asterism with the moon is prescribed for half the month;
for within a single month of Siṃha, there occurs the possibility of two asterisms:
the conjunction of the eighth lunar day with Rohiṇī, and likewise the ninth lunar day with Rohiṇī.
The tenth lunar day conjoined with Rohiṇī, as well as the eighth conjoined with Mṛgaśīrṣa;

the ninth conjoined with Mṛgaśīrṣa, and the tenth joined with Mṛgaśīrṣa—having observed these astrological conjunctions (yogas), O bulls among the twice-born, [one should perform the rite]. || 29–30 ||
On the day of the special conjunction, one should perform that great festival;
O twice-born ones, if one obtains that time of conjunction twice,
one should first perform it in the month of Siṃha and then perform the other.
For those who have taken initiation into the performance of desireless action (niṣkāma-karma) with the bear as their preeminent deity,
there shall indeed be victory for those who have sought refuge by following the path declared in the scriptures;
however, this is not so for Vaiṣṇavas on this earth who are intent upon actions performed for specific desires (kāmya-karma).
O lords of sages, I shall now declare the determination of Janmāṣṭamī:
the eighth lunar day (Aṣṭamī) conjoined with Rohiṇī and Mṛgaśīrṣa;
and the ninth lunar day (Navamī) conjoined with Rohiṇī and Mṛgaśīrṣa.
The Rohiṇī-daśamī and likewise the Mṛga-daśamī—
having observed these conjunctions as being free from the defect of overlap (viddha),
one should determine the distinction between the preceding and the succeeding [tithis] in their proper order. || 35-36 ||
O twice-born ones, when one obtains the most excellent conjunction for the performance of the festival on two occasions, one should abandon the former and observe it on the latter;
O lords of self-restraint, this applies even when the eighth lunar day is joined with the previous tithi.
One should perform this great festival on a Monday;
likewise, one should celebrate the festival of Kṛṣṇa’s birth every year.
Furthermore, everyone should perform this great festival at midnight.
In a temple there is a special distinction, whereas for a house it is said to be general;
because Vāsudeva himself is the direct teacher of the world,
he is the bestower of the final half [of liberation] in that birth.
All Vaiṣṇavas in the world should indeed perform this great festival;
having fasted on this day, one should break the fast at night.
For this follows immediately after the birth festival of the God of gods, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow.
On this day of breaking the fast, one should never entertain doubts regarding improper time or other such matters;
for he who does not perform this festival of Kṛṣṇa’s birth with devotion becomes a traitor to his guru,
a traitor to the gods, and a traitor to his master.
On that day, no other work whatsoever should be performed on the surface of the earth;
likewise,
for him whose anniversary (sapiṇḍīkaraṇa) falls on this very day, there shall never be any greater spiritual merit than that of performing the Śrāddha for his ancestors and other rites.
Whether in the forenoon or the afternoon, without failing to perform this great festival,
one should satisfy one's ancestors with food offered to the Blessed One.
Starting from the day of Śrī’s birth, one may observe this for a month or even for a fortnight.
For eleven days, nine days, five days, or even three days,
one should perform that great festival according to the extent of one's resources,
with the dramatic performances of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes as well as his congregational chanting (saṃkīrtana). || 47-48 ||

O best of the wise, one should perform the birth festival of the Lord of Śrī every year with daily village festivals, other displays of magnificence, gifts of food reaching down to the outcaste (Caṇḍāla), and great enjoyments. 49.
O best of sages, in whatever region on earth this festival of Daṃśaura does not take place,
there will certainly be drought in that land;
I shall now declare the definitive rules for the festival of the Illustrious Goddess.
On the ninth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Āśvina,
a great festival must be celebrated every year on this earth for Vīralakṣmī,
since she is the mother of those who possess a human form. (52)
Therefore, for her complete gratification, this festival must be performed;
among all other festivals in the world, it shall be the most preeminent.
Consequently, by all who have taken refuge [in her], it should be observed both in temples and in homes.
One should perform this great festival with pure devotion;
first, having ascertained that the ninth day (navamī) is free from even a fraction of the eighth day (aṣṭamī),
one should then celebrate this great festival on that [ninth] day.

One should perform the nine-day festival according to the sequence of the days, provided it is endowed with the fourfold offerings and distinguished as appropriate to the occasion (56). It is taught that the festival begins on the new moon day (amāvāsyā), even if it is devoid of a lunar day (tithi) [conjunction]. (57)
Starting from the second day of the bright fortnight, one should perform that great festival;
and according to the scriptures, one should daily perform the worship in four locations. On the ninth day, one should indeed [worship] Śrī, who resides within the pitcher, the fire, and the mandala.
Having offered the image according to the prescribed rite, O Goddess, one should perform a great festival.
In whatever country this festival takes place every year, in that country there shall be prosperity and good fortune in every respect. || 59-60 ||
The wise know the tenth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Āśvina to be Vijayā;
on that very day, one should perform the festival of the God's victory.
However, it should always be avoided if it is pierced by even a fraction of the ninth day.
On the tenth lunar day joined with the asterism Parva-vedha, one should perform the festival;
however, even if it is joined with the asterism Śravaṇa, one should abandon it if it is overlapped by the preceding day (pūrva-viddhā).
For the worship of Aparājitā, there should be an abundance of the asterism Śravaṇa on that ground.
Likewise, the evening time on the day of the New Moon (Atidhi) is inauspicious for a journey;
furthermore, it is unsuitable for the festival of Śrī Vāsudeva on the earth.
For the purpose of the King's coronation, a date joined with the previous tithi (pūrvaviddhā) is also condemned.

One should abandon the tenth day and accept only the pure [eleventh]. If there should be a loss of the lunar day (tithi) on the ninth day such that the tenth exists for even a single muhūrta on the following day, then one should not accept it. || 65-66 ||
On the eleventh day (Ekādaśī), one should perform that great festival for Śrī Viṣṇu;
this should never be done on the previous day when it is overlapped by the tenth (Daśamī),
O best of sages, for the sake of the prosperity of the king and the kingdom.
When, however, there is the occurrence of two tenth days for those whose intellects are obscured by ignorance,
then, having abandoned the first [tenth], one should perform the festival on the second;
and on the ninth day, O Great Earth, the worship should be completed.
On the tenth day, one should indeed perform the preliminary consecration (adhivāsana) of the weapons;
on the second remaining day, however, one should perform the festival along with the Śamī tree.
O best of sages, one should act thus for the sake of the welfare of the world.
I shall now fully declare the determination of the kindling of the Kṛttikās;
O wise ones, when the sun is in Scorpio during the month of Kārtika,
on the full moon day under the asterism of Kṛttikā at evening time, O Lord of Śrī.

Having decorated the temple on all sides with lamps, the king should cause a great festival to be held every year on earth for the prosperity of his kingdom. O wise ones, this should be done when the month of Kārttika has the sign of Scorpio (Vṛścika).

One should perform [the rites] in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa because of the excess of the month of Vṛścika. When there are two full-moon days (paurṇamāsī) in the month of Vṛścika, then one should abandon the first pair of asterisms (ṛkṣa) and proceed with the subsequent ones.
If the fourteenth day is pierced by [the previous tithi] and Kṛttikā is defiled,
one should perform this great festival on the full moon day when Rohiṇī is present.
If the full moon is joined with the fourteenth day, [one should act accordingly].
Therefore, one should indeed undertake this great festival on the first day (pratipad) of the lunar fortnight;
however, when the full moon (pūrṇimā) is defiled by Mars (Bhauma) and thus coincides with the pratipad,
one should abandon that day and perform it on the following day.
If the full moon day, Kṛttikā, Rohiṇī,
and the first lunar day (pratipat) are all joined with [the previous tithi] as viddha, then it is pure even when Mṛgaśiras is present.
On the second lunar day, one should indeed perform the great festival of lighting lamps.

The *saṃkrama* (the sun's passage) that is pierced in four ways should always be avoided on earth. However, if this [piercing] occurs from the other side—that is, from the east—one should perform a festival for Śauri, as the lighting of lamps is auspicious. 80–81.
Thus, for one who performs this great festival on earth with full devotion,
his desired goals will surely be accomplished without delay.
O best of sages, such is the definitive conclusion regarding Jayantī and the other festivals.
"That which was spoken by Nārāyaṇa himself in the past to the Lotus-born [Brahmā].
83. Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled "The Determination of the Festivals of Jayantī and Others," in the *Śrī-paramapuruṣa-saṃhitā*, within the *Rahasyasāra* of the *Śrī-pāñcarātra-āgama*.
The Sages:

O Lord of Munis, O highly fortunate one, how did the Ekādaśī vow originate in this world, O Sage, for those intent on the meditation of Śrī Hari? How is this vow to be performed, and what fruit is obtained by its performance?
"O ocean of mercy, tell us how that determination may come to pass.
Śrī Nārada replied:
"O sages, listen now to the cause for attaining Vaikuṇṭha."
It bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation in this world and the next;
it is endowed with great majesty, is a means of crossing the ocean of existence,
and contains the glory of Ekādaśī as well as the procedure for its vow.
Today I shall speak according to my ability, just as I heard it in the past from Indra,
concerning those gods who were defeated by the high-souled Dūrvāsas and who incurred a terrible curse from him.

Wandering through the forest, they were subjected to great sufferings. But having reached the Ocean of Milk, they meditated with steady minds upon Vāsudeva, the Lord of the Universe, by means of the Puruṣasūkta alone.

O twice-born ones, they performed extremely difficult penance for many thousands of years; nevertheless, even so, they did not obtain a vision of Hari. Consequently, the thirty gods became exceedingly distressed, O Samba.
Beholding them, the Lord, the Blessed One, the husband of Pārvatī, was moved by compassion.
He spoke these very sweet words to one among the gods:
"O gods, listen today to my great and pleasing speech.
Long ago, I heard this from a deer, which grants the fulfillment of all goals."
"The Ekādaśī vow is the most excellent of all in the three worlds. You should observe this one known as Harivāsara;
by that, the Lord of the World, being pleased, will himself grant you his vision."
"Therefore, your desired goal shall be accomplished; of this there is no doubt.
Thus did Śrī Śaṅkara speak to all the gods.
"If one should perform the Ekādaśī vow with devotion according to the scriptures," [so it was said].
Then, having descended from that state, he became directly and perceptibly manifest before the wise ones.
Seeing him, the thirty gods prostrated themselves like a staff upon the ground and made their petition to him,
detailing their suffering in full.
Having heard that, Hari, the lord of Ramā and an ocean of compassion, spoke these words—profound, fruitful, and great—to Vāca:
"Listen, all you gods; this shall bring about the fulfillment of your desired purpose."
I shall now describe at length a single, easily accessible means of accomplishment:
on this earth there is a great king of serpents named Mandhara;
it is there that the one known as Vāsuki resides.
And here, having taken it and cast it into the ocean of milk,
you shall churn it and then obtain the Kalpa-tree and other such things;
furthermore, you shall achieve the nectar of immortality, which is most difficult for the world to attain.
"By drinking which you shall become free from old age and death, and likewise endowed with exceptional fortitude, true heroism, and prowess;
however, do not desire friendship with the host of Dānavas. (20-21)
"O sages, while you perform this destruction of Madhu with those [weapons] joined together,
if not, then that task must be accomplished by us alone.
Having thus commanded them, Śauri then vanished on the spot.
Then the thirty-three gods, bearing the head [of Mahiṣa] at Hari's command,
churned the Ocean of Milk and obtained their desires;
from that time forth, the excellent vow of Hari’s day has been established throughout all the worlds.
O Sage, this vow which you have described brings pleasure to Hari and fulfills the desires of His devotees;
he who performs this vow, whether with desire or without desire, being dear to Hari,
shall enjoy all happiness and at the end attain Vaikuṇṭha.
On the morning of the tenth day,
having meditated upon Śrī Hari, the Lord of the worlds, O best of Ramās, for your pleasure I shall today observe the vow of Ekādaśī, O ocean of compassion. (26–27)
"O Lord of Gods, if you have compassion for me, grant that there be no obstacle.
Having thus petitioned with devotion, one should avoid eating at night,
sleep upon a bed of darbha grass, and meditate with fortitude on Śrī Hari.
Then, having risen at dawn and performed his ablutions and other rites accordingly,

he should worship the Lord with special reverence through the fourfold modes of adoration. Having accepted the holy water and the sacred earth of the shrine, he should perform the chanting of the names of Hari and so forth.
O twice-born ones, one should pass that day with the recitation of the Gītā and likewise the recitation of the Vedas;
having fasted, one should keep a vigil during that night,
avoiding perfumes, flowers, betel, and sexual union with women.
On the eleventh day, one should discard other fragrant substances.
O twice-born ones, that deluded soul in this world who, having fasted on the eleventh day, does not consume the prasāda of Mahāviṣṇu, [is lost].
For such a person, this entire vow certainly becomes fruitless.
Therefore, O Brahmins, with every effort, one should eat even a single grain of Hari’s prasāda on the eleventh day, but one should not eat more than that.
Indeed, on that day, food is not offered even to those of superior intellect.
O twice-born ones, if the Śrāddha for the ancestors or other rites should fall on that very day of Ekādaśī, one should not perform them; rather, one should perform them on the Dvādaśī.
On that day, women, children, the elderly, and those who are physically incapable should avoid eating;
instead, they should consume cow’s milk, fruits, and roots.
Furthermore, those who are unable to perform the night vigil on that day [should likewise observe these restrictions].
O lords of sages, one should spend as much time as possible during the night chanting the names of Śrī Hari and engaging in conversations about Him;
however, on the Ekādaśī day, one must not cut Tulasī leaves upon the ground.
The lifespan and prosperity of that person of deluded soul who performs [these acts] perish; however, for such a person,
the worship of the Śālagrāma, the giving of gifts, and the observance of the Ekādaśī day yield special fruits for men, granting the fulfillment of all desires.
Then, O Brahmins, on the twelfth day, at the interval of six ghaṭikās after sunrise,
he himself honored the Vaiṣṇavas who were devoted and surrendered to him with foodstuffs such as edibles and non-edibles, along with the grace of the waters from the Hari-tīrtha. || 41-42 ||
Having worshipped [the deity] and offered libations, he himself should eat the remainder at home;
sleeping during midday and eating at night on that day takes away the entire fruit of Ekādaśī— of this there is no doubt.
Therefore, on that very twelfth day, one should likewise sleep at midday;
O best of sages, one should also avoid eating during the night.
He who performs this vow entirely according to the injunctions of the scriptures [attains the fruit].
Having obtained all that is desired here, one shall go to the city of Vaikuṇṭha.
Hereafter, I shall proclaim the definitive determination of Ekādaśī,
hearing which men are liberated from the terrible cycle of existence in every respect.
O Brahmins, for this vow, the three days beginning with the tenth—namely the eleventh and the twelfth—are always suitable;
however, it may happen that on the tenth day, it is pierced by the ninth. 47–48.
The fast should be observed on the twelfth day, and the breaking of the fast (pāraṇa) on the thirteenth; however,
if the eleventh day is seen to be overlapped by the tenth,
one should abandon that day and fast on the following one.
O twice-born ones, when there is even a fraction of the twelfth day on the thirteenth day as well,
one should observe the fast as a complete twelfth day and arrange for the other half [of the ritual].
When the tenth, eleventh, and twelfth days constitute three full days, [the fast is complete].
O Brahmins, if even a single moment of the twelfth lunar day is defiled by the rising of dawn (aruṇodaya) or other such times,
one should arrange for half of the fast on that day and perform the ritual breaking of the fast (pāraṇa) according to the rules on the thirteenth day.
O lords of self-restraint, if for reasons such as greed or pride one performs this vow on the earth on a day already pierced by the previous tithi— whether it be the ninth, the eleventh,
or even the twelfth— [the result is as follows].
Furthermore, all the merit previously acquired by him perishes,
and this vow certainly becomes fruitless.
Therefore, [one should observe it] on the pure tenth day and likewise on the eleventh.
O lords of sages, one should indeed perform this vow on the twelfth day (dvādaśī).
However, if none of these [lunar days] are available, or if even one is defiled,
one should perform it on the eleventh, the twelfth, or the thirteenth day.
O best of the twice-born, he who performs this vow in accordance with the prescribed injunctions—
All these desired objects of his shall indeed be accomplished; there is no doubt in this matter.
Furthermore, he shall attain union (sāyujya) with the illustrious Viṣṇu on this earth.
Therefore, this vow should be observed by all devotees and Vaiṣṇavas.

Or indeed, it should be performed even by those free from desire solely for the pleasure of the Blessed One. O twice-born ones, he who would abandon this vow for any reason whatsoever shall not attain liberation through any means.

The Uddaya-ekādaśī and likewise the Śayana-ekādaśī are both most excellent; therefore, one should not abandon them. And on this earth, the Ekādaśī preceded by the word "Vaikuṇṭha" (Vaikuṇṭha-ekādaśī) is likewise supreme. || 61-62 ||
O lords of sages, this vow should be observed by all men;
even by a single person on earth, one may obtain the fruit of a full year.
On the eleventh day of the dark fortnight in the month of Dhanus, [one should worship] the Lord of Śrī.
One should properly perform the festival for the one preceded by the word "Vaikuṇṭha.
O wise ones, if there should be two Ekādaśīs in a single month,
then one should set aside the first and perform the festival on the second.
When there occurs the conjunction of the second Ekādaśī with the Saṃkramaṇa [of the sun],
then one should perform the great festival of the Lord of Śrī on the first day.
O lords of sages, he who gives up his own body on the Ekādaśī [attains liberation].

Such a person shall not go to the abode of Śrī Hari, which is difficult even for yogīs to attain. O lords of sages, such is the procedure and the definitive conclusion regarding this vow known as Harivāsara, the Ekādaśī.
"By the mere hearing of which all men on this earth cross over the ocean of worldly existence and attain the abode of Hari.
Thus spoke the silent sage Nārada to those foremost among the self-controlled.
The secret of the Blessed One’s teaching, which was formerly spoken by the Blessed One out of compassion to the Creator (Brahmā), and which Brahmā himself heard in its entirety and then,
likewise out of compassion, imparted to us— [that we have now received].
This compendium, consisting of one thousand verses, is dear to Hari;
among all the Saṃhitās, it is the best, concerning the Supreme Person.
Having heard this, all those lords of the self-restrained were likewise delighted in their hearts.

Having bowed down again and again to Nārada, the foremost of devotees, the chief of sages, and the beloved of the world, he worshipped him according to his desire. Thus honored by the silent sage, Nārada [addressed] the Lord of Śrī.
Meditating within his own heart upon Him and personally chanting His names,
he departed toward his own hermitage while delivering all the worlds.
Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Greatness of the Ekādaśī Vow," in the Śrī Paramapuruṣa Saṃhitā, which is the Essence of the Secrets of the Śrī Pañcarātra Āgama.
